The excuse ends in a plea: "Will you then destroy us for the falsehood they invented?’”" No one can shelter behind the errors of his forefathers.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Nor say, ‘It was our forefathers who had associated others ˹with Allah in worship˺"** They would claim that their fathers were idolaters before their time, and that it was their fathers who broke the covenant and pledge before them.

**"and we, as their descendants, followed in their footsteps."** They were only their offspring, small and weak, coming after them, and they simply copied them.

**"Will you then destroy us for the falsehood they invented?’”"** Would Allah punish them for what the idolaters among their forefathers did, when they set up idolatry and broke the covenant? They would plead: "O our Lord! Will You destroy us for what our ancestors did, and make our deeds worthless because they associated others with You?" They would insist they bore no sin, since they only followed their ancestors and had no knowledge.

### Why is imitation no excuse?

The verse denies them any refuge in the claim that they were unaware of the truth. They might argue that, as their forefathers' offspring, they only followed their path, so they should not be punished for their forefathers' error. The verse answers that they will not be punished for what their forefathers did. It was their own fault and their own indifference that brought them to ruin.

The covenant had sown the seed of truth in their hearts. So it was not hard for them to see that stones they had carved into idols, or fire, trees and other created things, could never be their Creator or help them in need. They cannot use such arguments, since they were made to testify within themselves to the oneness of Allah, tawḥīd. The reminder given through the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ, who brought the miracle, serves every soul as a call to remember that testimony within itself.

### The voice of inner nature

If an animal is taken from its parents and raised in an unfamiliar setting, it still keeps the traits of its species when it grows up. Its behaviour in everything springs from instinct. The same is true of a human being's awareness of Allah. The consciousness of a Creator and Lord is planted so deeply in the human soul that it is never lost.

But there is one difference between animals and humans. Animals cannot go against their nature. They are driven to do whatever their inner nature urges. A human being is different. This awareness lies in his nature, yet he is entirely free to act, even while his mind and conscience show him right and wrong. So he has the power and the choice either to follow his inner voice, or to ignore it and do as he likes.

It is in these moments of moral choice that a person is on trial, and on their outcome Paradise or Hell is decided. Whoever heeds Allah's voice, obeying what He commands in nature's silent language, passes the test. The doors of Paradise will be opened to him after death. Whoever ignores Allah's voice speaking through nature will be guilty in His sight, and Allah will ignore him just as he ignored that voice.

### In short

- No one may excuse his idolatry by saying he only followed his forefathers.
- Each person is answerable for his own choices, because the covenant planted the truth of tawḥīd in every heart.
- Unlike animals, humans are free to follow or ignore their inner voice, and that choice is their test.

174.text:
Verse 174 closes this passage: "This is how We make our signs clear, so perhaps they will return ˹to the Right Path˺". Allah sets out His signs in detail so that people may turn back to the pledge they made and acknowledge Him as their Lord.

### Phrase by phrase

**"This is how We make our signs clear,"** In the Qur'an Allah explains the story of the Covenant, and He makes His other signs clear in the same way. Just as He made His signs and proofs clear to earlier nations, He makes the lessons clear to these people, the Quraish.

**"so perhaps they will return ˹to the Right Path˺"**: so that they may reflect on them and turn back from disbelief and idolatry to the original Covenant. They may then repent of worshipping others alongside Allah and come to believe in Him alone and worship Him alone, as they had agreed long before they broke their promise.

### Who is left without an excuse?

Allah has made His signs plain through these detailed verses to make it easy for people to return to their pledge. Whoever applies his mind will find the truth and so escape everlasting punishment.

The voice of inner nature is itself evidence that Allah exists. So no one now has the excuse of ignorance. No one can say he is only doing what has been done since ancient times. A person brings the awareness of Allah with him from birth, and it survives every change in his circumstances. In view of this, what excuse does anyone have for following the path of misguidance?

### In short

- Allah explains the Covenant and His other signs in detail so that people may return to Him.
- The Quraish, like every nation, were shown these signs so that they would leave idolatry for worship of Allah alone.
- With the awareness of Allah born in every person, no one is left with an excuse for misguidance.

175.text:
Allah tells His Prophet ﷺ to relate a warning drawn from history: "And relate to them ˹O Prophet˺ the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he abandoned them, so Satan took hold of him, and he became a deviant". These verses concern an Israelite religious leader, widely followed for his learning and devotion, who suddenly strayed and ended among the rejected. The event holds many lessons. It also links with what came before. The preceding verses spoke of the covenant Allah made with the children of Adam in general, and with particular people in various circumstances. They also mentioned those who did not keep their pledge with Allah. An example is the Israelites, who awaited a prophet and described his qualities to others, yet rejected him for worldly reasons once the Holy Prophet ﷺ appeared.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And relate to them ˹O Prophet˺"** Recite, O Muhammad, to the Jews, the Israelites. The Prophet ﷺ was asked to tell his people this story. It shows how a devoted scholar and great spiritual leader lost all his knowledge, wisdom, popularity and fame simply by following worldly desires.

**"the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs,"** The man was one of the Israelites to whom Allah gave His signs, so that he knew and understood the truth they pointed to. He had knowledge of certain books Allah had revealed, and "Our signs" refers to that knowledge. One explanation says the signs were Allah's Greatest Name.

**"but he abandoned them,"** He did not act on them. He left them and moved away from them. The Qur'an pictures this as "wriggling out", like a snake leaving its old skin behind with no further concern for it. So he cast off the knowledge and wisdom Allah had given him and emerged in disbelief.

**"so Satan took hold of him,"** Satan pursued and caught up with him and became his close companion, deluding him. As long as he held the knowledge of Allah's signs, Satan could not take hold of him. As soon as he lost that great gift, Satan overtook him and led him astray.

**"and he became a deviant"**: he joined the erring disbelievers who go astray and are ruined, after having been rightly guided and on the path to salvation.

### Who was he?

The Holy Qur'an gives no name or identifying detail for this person. Many Traditions, however, from the Companions, their disciples and the interpreters of the Qur'an, give varied information about him. ʿAbdur-Razzāq recorded that ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said the verse is about Balʿam ibn Bāʿūrāʾ, a man of the children of Israel. Another report from Ibn Masʿūd names him Balʿam ibn Abrah. In one report Ibn ʿAbbās said he was Ṣayfī, son of ar-Rāhib. Kaʿb said he was a man from al-Balqāʾ, a province of Jordan, who knew Allah's Greatest Name and lived in Jerusalem with the tyrants. Al-ʿAwfī reported Ibn ʿAbbās saying he was Balʿam ibn Bāʿūrāʾ, a man from Yemen to whom Allah had given knowledge of His signs, but who abandoned them. Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah said the same.

According to Mālik ibn Dīnār, he was an Israelite scholar whose supplication Allah used to answer. People would ask him to lead them in supplication in times of hardship. Mūsā (Moses) sent him to invite the king of Madyan to Allah. The king won him over with land and gifts, and he abandoned Mūsā's religion for the king's.

So, as Ibn Masʿūd and several others among the Salaf held, the verse is well known to concern an ancient man from the children of Israel. The Tradition that most scholars consider most authentic and reliable is the one Ibn Marduwaih reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās. It says his name was Balʿam ibn Bāʿūrāʾ, from Syria, living in Canaan near Jerusalem, and by one report an Israelite by birth.

Another view, held by ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and Zayd ibn Aslam, is that the verse came down about Umayyah ibn Abī as-Ṣalt al-Thaqafī. A student of the Scriptures, he knew a messenger was due to be sent about then, and hoped the choice would fall on him. When Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, he envied him bitterly and disbelieved in him. One explanation calls him Umayyah ibn al-Ṣalt and says Allah had honoured him with knowledge and eloquence, then took them away when he refused to believe.

### Balʿam and the city of the tyrants

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah al-Wālibī reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that the man came from the city of the tyrants, the Jabbārīn, which is Jerusalem. His name was Balʿam, and he knew Allah's Greatest Name. When Mūsā and those with him came to that city, Balʿam's cousins and his people came to him. They said Mūsā was a strong man with a huge army, and if he defeated them they would be destroyed. So he should pray to Allah to keep Mūsā and his followers from overcoming them. Balʿam replied that if he prayed for that, he would lose both this world and the next. But they kept pressing him until he prayed against Mūsā and his people, and Allah stripped him of what He had given him. Hence Allah's words "but he abandoned them, so Satan took hold of him".

### The story as Ibn ʿAbbās told it

According to Ibn Marduwaih's report, these events came after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people and the Israelites' deliverance from Egypt. Allah commanded Mūsā and his people to fight a people called the Jabbārīn. The Jabbārīn had seen what became of Pharaoh's people, and they were terrified when they saw Mūsā's army approach. They came to Balʿam and told him that Mūsā was a powerful man who had come with a great army to drive them from their land. He should pray to Allah to turn them back without a fight. Balʿam was known to know the Greatest Name of Allah, and his prayers made through it were usually granted.

Balʿam told them that Mūsā, as Allah's prophet, had the support of Allah's angels, so he could not pray against him. He knew Mūsā's rank with Allah, and praying against him would ruin him in this world and the next. When they insisted, he promised to seek Allah's permission first, and to pray against Mūsā only if Allah allowed it. He did something to seek Allah's consent, and in a dream Allah forbade him to make such a prayer. He told the people of this prohibition.

The Jabbārīn then gave him a valuable gift, which he accepted, and after that they pressed him even harder. Some reports say his wife urged him to accept the gift and pray for them. Blinded by love of wealth and of his wife, he began to pray against Mūsā and his people. Then something unusual happened. By Allah's will, every curse he meant for Mūsā came out against the Jabbārīn themselves. They cried out and rebuked him for cursing them. He said he could not utter a word against Mūsā and had no control over what he said.

The Jabbārīn were then destroyed by a punishment from heaven. Balʿam's punishment was that his tongue hung out of his mouth until it dangled on his chest. Having ruined his life in this world and the next, and stripped of all his spiritual powers, he made a suggestion to the Jabbārīn. They could defeat the Israelites only one way. They should dress up their beautiful girls and send them among the Israelites with orders not to resist whatever was done to them. Far from home, the Israelites were likely to fall into adultery. Adultery is the act Allah hates most and must draw His wrath, and an adulterous people can never defeat its enemy.

The people accepted this satanic plan and carried it out. A prominent Israelite fell into the trap. Mūsā did all he could to stop him, but he went ahead with the shameful act. A plague then struck them as punishment, and seventy thousand people died in a single day. The Israelites killed the man who had sinned, along with the girl, and hung them up in a public place. After that they repented to Allah and sought His forgiveness, and He relieved them of the shameful punishment.

### The wasted prayers of al-Basūs

ʿIkrimah reported from Ibn ʿAbbās a different account. The verse concerns a man who was granted three prayers that would be answered. He had a wife named al-Basūs, who loved him and bore him children. One day she asked him to use one of his prayers for her. He agreed and asked what she wanted. She asked him to pray that Allah make her the most beautiful woman among the children of Israel. When she saw that no one could match her, she turned away from him and wanted another life. So he prayed that Allah would turn her into a barking dog, and two of his prayers were gone.

Then her children came to him. They could not bear it, they said, since their mother had become a barking dog and people insulted them because of her. They asked him to pray that Allah restore her. He prayed, and she became as she had been. So all three answered prayers were wasted. This is the al-Basūs whose ill luck became proverbial, so that people say of someone that he or she is unluckier than al-Basūs.

### In short

- The Prophet ﷺ was told to relate the story of a man given Allah's signs who cast them off as a snake sheds its skin.
- Most reports name him Balʿam ibn Bāʿūrāʾ, an Israelite scholar who knew Allah's Greatest Name. Another view names Umayyah ibn Abī as-Ṣalt.
- Pressed by his people, won over by a gift and urged by his wife, he prayed against Mūsā, but his curses turned on his own side.
- Once he lost the knowledge of Allah's signs, Satan overtook him, and he even devised a plan to lure the Israelites into sin.

176.text:
Allah describes what Balʿam could have become, and what he chose instead: "If We had willed, We would have elevated him with Our signs, but he clung to this life—following his evil desires." Then comes the image: "His example is that of a dog: if you chase it away, it pants, and if you leave it, it ˹still˺ pants." The verse widens the lesson: "This is the example of the people who deny Our signs. So narrate ˹to them˺ stories ˹of the past˺, so perhaps they will reflect".

### Phrase by phrase

**"If We had willed, We would have elevated him with Our signs,"** Through the signs He had taught him, Allah would have raised him above the filth of this worldly life. He would have let him benefit from them and act on them, raising him in this world and the next. One explanation says Allah would have raised him to heaven through the Greatest Name and made him a ruler over the people of the world. Another says He would have raised him to the ranks of the scholars by easing his way to good deeds.

**"but he clung to this life"** The verb akhlada means to incline toward something or cling to it. Literally, he clung to the earth. The word for earth, arḍ, covers the globe and everything on it. Furniture, machines, clothes and food are all gifts of the earth, so the one word stands for all worldly possessions. He was drawn to the adornment and delights of this life. He indulged in its pleasures and was deceived by it, as it deceives others like him who lack sound understanding.

**"—following his evil desires."** He followed his craving for leadership, or the lusts of his ego in doing evil, and called others to them. So Allah brought him low. He chose what led to his failure, preferring worldly desires to the Hereafter. The heart of the verse is that knowledge of Allah's signs is the real source of honour and advancement. For those who disregard them and prefer worldly desires and possessions, that very knowledge becomes a source of disgrace and disaster.

**"His example is that of a dog:"** His description, in his extreme greed for this world, is like a dog's. The likeness is Balʿam's, or by another explanation that of Umayyah ibn al-Ṣalt. The "therefore" that opens this clause in the Arabic ties it to what came before, his leaning toward this world and following his whims. So the likeness is in condition and in baseness.

**"if you chase it away, it pants, and if you leave it, it ˹still˺ pants."** The word lahath means to breathe hard with the tongue hanging out. Breathing in fresh air and breathing out stale air is vital to every living creature. Allah has made it automatic and effortless for all of them except the dog. The dog alone must labour to breathe, while other animals do so only when attacked or straining. No other animal is like it in this. Whether driven off or left alone, its tongue lolls out in disgrace. Balʿam is likened to a dog because his tongue hung out and he panted like one.

**"This is the example of the people who deny Our signs."** These are the people who deny Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an, the Jews. Ibn ʿAbbās said this refers to the Israelites who had always longed for someone to be sent to them as a leader, to invite them to Allah and teach them the right path. When the long-awaited Prophet came with signs of truth so clear that they left no room for resistance, they too wriggled out of the Torah's commands, just as Balʿam had done.

**"So narrate ˹to them˺ stories ˹of the past˺, so perhaps they will reflect"** Recite the Qur'an to them, O Messenger, so that they may think about its parables, reject their denial of the truth and come to believe. Tell the story especially to the children of Israel, who knew what happened to Balʿam when Allah let him stray and expelled him from His mercy.

### What does the dog's panting stand for?

Scholars differ over the meaning of this parable. Some say it refers to Balʿam's tongue, which hung out of his mouth, as in the story narrated through Ibn Isḥāq, Sālim and Abū an-Naḍr. So he is like a dog whose tongue lolls whether it is chased away or not.

Others say it is a parable of this man, and those like him, in their misguidance. They persist on the wrong path and cannot benefit from faith or grasp what they are called to. Like a dog that pants whether chased or left alone, such a person gains nothing from advice or the call to faith. It is as if he had never been advised at all. Allah says in other verses: "As for those who persist in disbelief, it is the same whether you warn them or not—they will never believe" (2:6). And: "Even if you pray for their forgiveness seventy times, Allah will never forgive them." (9:80).

A third view holds that the wicked, the hypocrite and the disbeliever all have a weak heart, empty of guidance, which keeps faltering. A similar view was narrated from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī. One explanation applies the parable to both Balʿam and Umayyah: when they were admonished they paid no heed, and when they were left alone they understood nothing.

### The donkey that would not go on

Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn Yasār narrated, through Sālim, from Abū an-Naḍr, a fuller account. When Mūsā (Moses) entered the land of the Canaanites in ash-Shām, Greater Syria, Balʿam's people came to him. They said that Mūsā son of ʿImrān had come with the children of Israel to drive them out of their land, kill them and settle the Israelites in their place. They had nowhere else to live. Since his supplication was answered, he should go out and pray against them.

Balʿam answered: woe to you! This is Allah's Prophet, and the angels and the believers are with him. How can I pray against them when I know from Allah what I know? But they kept saying they had nowhere else to go, coaxing and begging him until he gave in to the temptation. He rode his donkey toward Mount Ḥusbān, behind the Israelite camp. After a while the donkey sat down and refused to go on. He dismounted and beat it until it got up, and he rode on. A little later the donkey did the same, and again he beat it until it rose.

When he went on and tried to curse Mūsā and his people, Allah made his tongue speak ill of his own people and well of the children of Israel. His people protested that he was praying for the Israelites and against them. He said it was against his will, a matter Allah had decided. Then, with his tongue hanging out of his mouth, he told them that he had now lost this world and the Hereafter. It was about this story of Balʿam son of Bāʿūrāʾ that the verse came down.

### Why was the story told to the Israelites?

Allah had favoured Balʿam by teaching him His Greatest Name. When Allah is asked by it He gives, and when He is called by it He answers. But Balʿam used it in disobedience to Allah. He invoked Allah against His own party, the people of faith who followed Mūsā son of ʿImrān, His servant and Messenger in that age, to whom Allah spoke directly. The story was told so that the Israelites would reflect and avoid what Balʿam did.

Allah gave the Jews knowledge and raised them above the bedouins around them. He gave them a description of Muhammad ﷺ that let them recognise him as they recognise their own children. Of all people they had the most right to follow, help and support Muhammad ﷺ, in obedience to their own prophets, who told them of him and commanded them to follow him. So any of them who goes against what their Books teach, or keeps it hidden from Allah's servants, will meet disgrace from Allah in this life and humiliation in the Hereafter.

### The man who wanted to be the prophet

In the Prophet's time there was a man of great moral and intellectual distinction named Umayyah ibn Abī as-Ṣalt. When he learned that the holy books of the Christians and Jews foretold a coming prophet, he believed he himself was that prophet. Later, when he heard of the Prophet Muhammad's claim and the fine discourse revealed to him, he was bitterly disappointed and turned into an opponent.

The proper use of Umayyah's fine gifts would have been to recognise Allah's Prophet and become his companion. But because Allah had already blessed him so much, he thought the blessing of prophethood should have come to him and no one else. He saw worldly gain in rejecting the Prophet, though accepting him would have brought gain in the Hereafter. Had he chosen to accept, he could have had the angels as companions on his journey. Once he took the path of jealousy and pride, Satan was his only companion.

This example applies to everyone who ignores the truth, or refuses it out of jealousy and arrogance. Such a person falls from the level of humanity to that of a dog. A dog pants whether it is treated well or badly, and so does he. When Allah blessed him, he grew arrogant, and when He withheld a blessing, he stayed arrogant. He should have been grateful to Allah for His blessing. When a blessing was withheld, he should have accepted Allah's decision and turned back to Him.

### In short

- Allah's signs would have raised Balʿam in both worlds, but he clung to the earth and its possessions and followed his desires.
- He is likened to a dog that pants whether chased or left alone, a picture of greed, of a tongue hanging out, and of a heart no advice can reach.
- The story was told to the Israelites, who knew the Prophet's description, so that they would not repeat Balʿam's betrayal.
- Whoever rejects the truth out of jealousy or pride, like Umayyah ibn Abī as-Ṣalt, falls from humanity to the level of a dog.

177.text:
Allah passes judgement on those the parable describes: "What an evil example of those who denied Our signs! They ˹only˺ wronged their own souls". Could anything be worse than a people who reject Allah's signs and proofs, wronging themselves by doing so and gaining only their own ruin?

### Phrase by phrase

**"What an evil example of those who denied Our signs!"** Those who deny Allah's signs, Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an, are likened to dogs, which care for nothing but finding food and satisfying their lusts. Anyone who steps outside knowledge and guidance to chase his cravings and whims is therefore no better than a dog. What an evil example that is. The Ṣaḥīḥ records that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that the evil example is not fitting for believers. One who takes back his gift is like a dog that returns to eat its own vomit.

**"They ˹only˺ wronged their own souls"** Allah did not wrong them. They wronged themselves by denying, rejecting guidance and disobeying their Lord. They were content with a life that will soon end, while chasing their desires and obeying their lusts. They harmed only themselves, bringing torment on themselves.

### What lessons does Balʿam's story teach?

This passage holds several useful lessons for those who take heed and use their understanding. They follow from the parable of the previous verse (7:176):

1. No one should boast of his knowledge or take pride in his piety. Things can change without warning, as they did for Balʿam ibn Bāʿūrāʾ. A person should thank his Lord for whatever knowledge and wisdom he has, and keep praying to Allah for firmness in faith.
2. One should avoid situations that threaten one's faith and knowledge. This is especially so where money, wife and children are involved, because love of these is the most powerful agent of misguidance.
3. One should avoid the company of the misguided and be careful about accepting their gifts or invitations. Balʿam met his evil end through accepting the gift of the Jabbārīn.
4. Shameless acts such as adultery and fornication bring ruin and disaster on the whole society. Those who want to save themselves from distress must stop their people from such crimes, or they will draw Allah's wrath and punishment on themselves.
5. Turning away from Allah's commands is itself a punishment. It opens the door to satanic influences, which work on people without their knowing and lead them astray. So anyone with knowledge must be aware of this precious treasure and seek Allah's help to protect it from evil influences. He must keep carefully correcting himself against error.

### In short

- Those who deny Allah's signs are like dogs that care only for food and lust, and the Prophet ﷺ said the believers must not fit such an evil example.
- Allah wronged them in nothing, for they harmed only themselves.
- Balʿam's fall warns against pride in knowledge, love of wealth and family, gifts from the misguided, and shamelessness, and calls for constant self-correction.

178.text:
The passage ends by tracing guidance and loss back to Allah: "Whoever Allah guides is truly guided. And whoever He leaves to stray, they are the ˹true˺ losers". The main theme of verse 178 is that guidance and misguidance both come from Allah. He is the Creator of good and evil, of guidance and misguidance.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Whoever Allah guides is truly guided."** Whoever Allah guides to His religion is truly guided, and no one can lead him astray. Such people are guided because they chose the path of their Lord.

**"And whoever He leaves to stray,"** Whoever Allah does not lead to His path, but turns away from it because of his deviation and bad deeds, has earned failure, loss and certain misguidance. Whatever Allah wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen.

**"they are the ˹true˺ losers"**: they will be punished, and they lose themselves and their families on the Day of Judgement. Is that not complete loss?

### Who chooses guidance?

The Qur'an returns to this theme in many verses, so that people may know that Allah created both good and evil. He gave clear instructions for telling one from the other, and a kind of free will to choose between the two paths. Those who freely choose the right path and do good are rewarded by Allah. Those who freely take the other path and do evil are punished and sent to Hell.

Allah does not appear openly to guide people. He shows them His way through signs. Guidance in this world comes to those able to see the truth in the form of signs and reasoning, and willing to yield to it. For those who give no weight to signs and arguments, nothing awaits but eternal ruin.

A hadith narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, the opening words of a sermon, puts this into words. It begins by praising Allah and asking His help, guidance and forgiveness, and by seeking refuge with Him from the evils within oneself and the burden of one's evil deeds. It continues: whomever Allah guides, no one can mislead, and whomever He leaves astray, no one can guide. It ends with the testimony that there is no god but Allah, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Imām Aḥmad, the compilers of the Sunan and others collected the full hadith.

### Why is "guided" singular and "losers" plural?

The verse speaks of the guided in the singular and of the misguided losers in the plural. This shows that the path of guidance is one true faith, followed by all the prophets from Adam to the last of the prophets ﷺ. The basic message of all the prophets has been the same, and its fundamentals were the same in every age. So people of any age or community who believed in their prophets and followed their teachings belong, in Allah's sight, to one and the same category: the guided. The paths of misguidance, by contrast, number in the thousands, so they are mentioned in the plural.

### Why is no reward mentioned for the guided?

The verse names the losers together with their punishment, but mentions no reward for the guided. It simply calls them "the guided". This implies that guidance itself is the greatest blessing of all, embracing every reward and favour in this world and the Hereafter. The reward of guidance needs no separate mention of the other rewards it contains.

Suppose a great king assures someone that he is the king's close friend, whose word will be heard and trusted. That person certainly holds the highest place among the royal officials and needs no formal rank or post. In the same way, whoever Allah has called "the guided" has received every reward. So the elders say that remembrance and worship of Allah are themselves the reward for worship, because they are Allah's great favour. Anyone engaged in worshipping Allah is receiving His greatest reward in that very moment. The other blessings waiting for him in this world and in Paradise come second, as the fruit of this guidance.

This also explains another verse, which promises the believers "a recompense from your Lord, a gift". Two different words describe their reward. Jazāʾ, recompense, is given in return for a service, while ʿaṭāʾ, a gift, is given with no service performed. So what people take to be the reward of their own deeds and achievements is in fact a gift from their Lord. The very deed that earned the reward was itself His gift, since He enabled them to perform it.

### In short

- Guidance and misguidance come from Allah, who created good and evil and gave people the free will to choose.
- "Guided" is singular because there is one true faith shared by all the prophets, while the paths of error are many.
- No reward is named for the guided because guidance is itself the greatest reward, and even good deeds are Allah's gift.

179.text:
The previous verse traced guidance and loss back to Allah. This one describes those who end in loss: "Indeed, We have destined many jinn and humans for Hell." Their faculties are intact, yet unused: "They have hearts they do not understand with, eyes they do not see with, and ears they do not hear with." So the verse judges them: "They are like cattle. In fact, they are even less guided! Such ˹people˺ are ˹entirely˺ heedless". Many jinn and humans are bound for Hell. They have all the means of guidance, hearts, eyes and ears, but never use them to seek it. Had they used these faculties properly, they could have found the right path.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, We have destined many jinn and humans for Hell."** Allah has set aside a share of the Fire for many jinn and humans, and Hell is their lot. He prepared them for it through their doing the deeds of its people. He made many of them for the Fire because He knew they would do the deeds of the people of Hell.

**"They have hearts they do not understand with,"** They do not use their hearts to grasp the truth, or to see what will benefit them and what will harm them.

**"eyes they do not see with,"** They do not see the proofs of Allah's power with the kind of sight that leads to reflection. They do not look at Allah's signs within themselves and on the horizons so as to learn from them.

**"and ears they do not hear with."** They do not listen to Allah's verses, signs and warnings in a way that leads them to think and take heed. They do not benefit from the senses Allah gave them as a means of guidance.

**"They are like cattle."** In failing to understand, see and listen, they are like grazing cattle, which use their senses only for what keeps them alive in this world. They neither hear nor understand the truth, nor see the guidance. Allah gives a similar example: "The example of the disbelievers ˹not responding to the Messenger’s warning˺ is like a flock not comprehending the calls and cries of the shepherd." (2:171). When such people are called to faith, they are like cattle that hear only their shepherd's voice without grasping what he says.

**"In fact, they are even less guided!"** They are further astray than cattle. Cattle at least answer their shepherd's call, even without understanding it. Cattle seek what benefits them and keep away from what harms them, while these people head for the Fire out of sheer obstinacy. Cattle also fulfil the purpose and service for which they were created. The disbeliever's purpose was the worship of Allah alone, in tawḥīd, yet he chose disbelief and gave Allah partners. Hence the obedient among people rank above some angels, whereas the disbelievers rank below cattle.

**"Such ˹people˺ are ˹entirely˺ heedless"**: oblivious to faith in Allah and the Last Day, and to the matter of the Hereafter, which they deny.

### Were they created for Hell?

When Allah willed to create His creation, He knew what they would do before they existed. Fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and the earth, He recorded all of it in a Book that is with Him. Muslim recorded from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that Allah fixed the destinies and measures of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, when His Throne was over the water. Many other hadiths deal with this subject. The question of al-Qadar, the divine decree, is of the greatest importance, but this verse is not the place for a full discussion of it.

The verse also teaches that a person's final end is a divine secret, known to no one. Yet there are clear signs from which one may form a judgement. The people of Hell can be recognised by one mark: they do not use their faculties of sight, hearing and understanding as they should. Allah gave people these faculties so that they could gain knowledge and come to know their Lord. The people of Hell spend them on worthless aims. They are plainly heedless of the real aim of human life, which is to use one's abilities to seek guidance and earn eternal comfort and peace in the Hereafter.

### Deaf, dumb and blind, but only to guidance

Allah says something similar of earlier nations: "And We gave them hearing, sight, and intellect. But neither their hearing, sight, nor intellect were of any benefit to them whatsoever, since they persisted in denying Allah’s signs." (46:26). Of the hypocrites He says: "They are ˹wilfully˺ deaf, dumb, and blind, so they will never return ˹to the Right Path˺" (2:18). And of the disbelievers: "˹They are wilfully˺ deaf, dumb and blind so they have no understanding" (2:171).

They are not actually deaf, dumb or blind, except where guidance is concerned. Allah says: "Had Allah known any goodness in them, He would have certainly made them hear. ˹But˺ even if He had made them hear, they would have surely turned away heedlessly" (8:23). And: "Indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but it is the hearts in the chests that grow blind" (22:46). The one who turns from remembrance of the Most Merciful is given a devil as a companion, who keeps him from the path while he thinks he is guided: "And whoever turns a blind eye to the Reminder of the Most Compassionate, We place at the disposal of each a devilish one as their close associate who will certainly hinder them from the ˹Right˺ Way while they think they are ˹rightly˺ guided" (43:36-37).

### If they can see and hear, why does the Qur'an deny it?

Someone may say that the Qur'an denies these people hearing, sight and understanding. Yet in real life they are not blind, deaf or mad. Like other people, they see, hear and understand the things around them. How can the two be reconciled?

The answer calls for a fresh look at the things and creatures around us. Everything created has as much awareness as its purpose requires. The things called inanimate are not wholly without awareness or life. Stones and soil, which have no task of growing or moving, have so little sensitivity that it can hardly be detected. Reason requires that even these have some kind of perception or life, since there must be some means of communication between the Creator and what He creates. A lord who could not communicate with what he made, because it had no awareness, would not be worthy of divinity. Allah does communicate with everything He has created, living or not, which shows that even lifeless things have some kind of awareness.

Plants come next. Their purpose calls for growth and nourishment, so they are given more perception, or life, matching their needs. Next comes the animal kingdom, where life is more developed and complex. Besides growing and feeding, animals must move from place to place, seek their food, protect themselves from danger and, above all, reproduce. So they are given more life, and more visibly, than the others. Yet they have only as much power as they need to feed themselves and guard against dangers and enemies.

Last of all comes the human being. Beyond all these functions, and above them, he has the duty of recognising his Creator, the Lord of the universe. He is to seek His pleasure by following His commands and avoiding what He dislikes. He must reflect on creation and use his reason to tell right from wrong, avoiding evil and doing good to please his Lord. He is also given vast scope to make his life more purposeful and raise his standing. As he progresses, he can rise higher than the angels. He is accountable for his deeds, promised eternal peace for good deeds and everlasting punishment for evil ones. So he has been entrusted with the highest and most perfect degree of life, to spend it on what suits the purpose of his life. He is not meant to waste his special faculties of understanding, hearing and sight on material things alone, as animals do.

So human understanding, hearing and sight should be distinct from those of animals. If a person does not use them for their special purpose, telling right from wrong, doing good and avoiding evil, he is rightly counted among those who have eyes but do not see, ears but do not hear, and hearts but do not understand. That is why the Holy Qur'an calls such people "deaf, dumb and blind".

### What did ʿĀd and Thamūd see?

The verse does not deny their physical ability to see, hear and understand. The Holy Qur'an even affirms their knowledge of worldly matters, in the verse quoted under 7:8 (30:7). Speaking of the destruction of the people of ʿĀd and of Thamūd, it says: "Satan made their ˹evil˺ deeds appealing to them, hindering them from the ˹Right˺ Way, although they were capable of reasoning" (29:38).

Lured by satanic influences, ʿĀd and Thamūd threw themselves into the evil deeds that destroyed them. They kept their abilities for base worldly gains, such as serving their bodily needs, and ignored the demands of the spirit. People may make great advances in science and technology. They may conquer space, explore the moon and other planets, fill the sky with sophisticated satellites and harness the forces of nature for their many needs. Yet all of this only serves their physical, material life. It does not reach beyond, to the search for spiritual peace and comfort.

Such achievements of science and technology serve the body alone, and in this respect do not set a person apart from an animal. That is why the Holy Qur'an calls such people deaf, dumb and blind. They heard, saw and understood only what belonged to this world. They did not put these faculties to the use that could lead them to eternal success and peace.

### Why are they worse than cattle?

The verse likens them to cattle because they spend all their effort on their bodily desires. It then adds that they are even further astray, far less wise than cattle. Animals are not bound by the laws of the Sharīʿah and receive no reward or punishment for what they do. They are required only to meet their physical needs, and they do so efficiently. Human beings, by contrast, are answerable for everything they do in this world and will be rewarded or punished accordingly. If they confine their efforts to worldly gain and fail to use their faculties properly, they are certainly more foolish than animals.

### Who finds the truth?

Truth is something each person must discover for himself. Allah has given everyone a heart, which is the mind, along with eyes and ears, and a person reaches the truth by using them. Whoever does not use them will never find the truth, however close it may be. Discovering the truth is each person's own conscious and deliberate act.

Only someone who keeps the doors of his heart open will understand the truth. Only someone who has not covered his eyes with artificial veils will see it. Only someone who has not stopped his ears will hear its voice. Such people recognise the voice of truth and surrender to it. Whoever is the opposite will stay mindless like the animals, and even the weightiest arguments will not move him. Flashes of Allah's brilliant light will appear before him, but he will not see them. The melody of the divine song will reach his ears, but he will be kept from hearing it. The truth is there for those who are awake. For the heedless, no truth is the Truth.

### In short

- Many jinn and humans are bound for Hell, as Allah knew and wrote long before creation, because they leave their hearts, eyes and ears unused for guidance.
- They are not physically blind or deaf. Like ʿĀd and Thamūd, they use their faculties only for worldly ends, which is no better than an animal's use.
- Humans hold the highest degree of life and are accountable under the Sharīʿah, so wasting their faculties puts them below cattle.
- Truth must be sought with an open heart, eyes and ears, and it is found only by those who are awake.

180.text:
After describing the heedless people of Hell, Allah points to the cure: "Allah has the Most Beautiful Names. So call upon Him by them, and keep away from those who abuse His Names. They will be punished for what they used to do". The people of Hell described above did not use their faculties to seek the lasting comforts of the Hereafter, and so made themselves liable to eternal punishment. This verse gives the remedy for their sickness. It is to seek Allah's help by calling on Him with His beautiful Names and remembering Him often through them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Allah has the Most Beautiful Names."** These are His loftiest attributes, such as knowledge, power, hearing and sight, which show His majesty and perfection. The Names are ninety-nine, as mentioned in a hadith. Al-ḥusnā, "most beautiful", is the feminine of al-aḥsan. The beautiful Names are those that denote attributes of the highest perfection, and perfection of the highest degree belongs to no one but Allah. Even a "perfect" human being may be surpassed by someone else in some quality, as the Qur'an says: "But above those ranking in knowledge is the One All-Knowing" (12:76).

**"So call upon Him by them,"** Invoke Him and recite them, and use them when asking Him for whatever you wish. The way the verse is worded shows that these beautiful Names belong to Allah alone. No one else has these attributes, so He alone deserves to be called on in need. "Calling" here has two aspects. One is praising, glorifying and remembering Allah. The other is calling on Him for help in need or difficulty. So Allah alone deserves praise and glorification, and He alone should be called on for help and relief. The verse also shows that the best way to call on Him is by His beautiful Names.

**"and keep away from those who abuse His Names."** The word for abusing is ilḥād, which means turning away from the centre. It also carries the senses of deviation, wickedness, injustice and straying. The niche in a grave is called laḥd for this reason: it is a hollow within a hollow, turned toward the qiblah. The verb can come from alḥada or from laḥada, and means those who turn away from the truth. In Qur'anic usage, ilḥād means departing from the correct meaning of the Qur'an's words or twisting its message. The Prophet ﷺ was told to keep away from those who distort Allah's prescribed Names or turn away from them.

Such people derived names for their gods from Allah's Names: al-Lāt from Allāh, al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz, "the Almighty", and Manāt from al-Mannān, "the Bestower of favours". Al-ʿAwfī reported that Ibn ʿAbbās said abusing Allah's Names includes claiming that al-Lāt was derived from Allah's Name. Ibn Jurayj narrated that Mujāhid said they derived al-Lāt from Allah and al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz. Qatādah said ilḥād means associating others with Allah in His Names, as in calling an idol al-ʿUzzā. Others say these are people who deny His Names and attributes, or distort their meanings, or give them to false deities. By another reading, they are people who refuse to acknowledge His Names. This was revealed before the command to fight them.

**"They will be punished for what they used to do"**: in the Hereafter Allah will repay them with a painful punishment for what they did and said in this world.

### How many Names does Allah have?

Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that Allah has ninety-nine Names, one hundred less one, and that Paradise is for whoever enumerates and safeguards them. Allah is Witr, One, and He loves al-Witr, what is odd in number. The two Ṣaḥīḥs collected this hadith, and al-Bukhārī and Muslim's version speaks of learning them by heart. At-Tirmidhī and al-Ḥākim listed these Names in detail. Prayers made by reciting them are usually answered.

Yet Allah's Names are not limited to ninety-nine. In his Musnad, Imām Aḥmad recorded from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught a supplication for anyone overwhelmed by sadness or grief. The person says that he is Allah's servant, the son of His servant, his forelock in His hand. Allah's decree concerning him will certainly come to pass, and His judgement on him is just. He then asks Allah by every Name He has, by which He named Himself, revealed in His Book, taught to any of His creatures, or kept with Himself in the knowledge of the Unseen. He asks Him to make the Glorious Qur'an the spring of his heart and the light of his chest, the remover of his sorrow and the dispeller of his worry. Allah will then take away his grief and sadness and replace them with joy. The Prophet ﷺ was asked whether they should learn these words. He said yes: everyone who hears this supplication should learn it.

### Why call on Allah alone?

The verse teaches two valuable things. First, no one but Allah deserves praise or deserves to be called on for help. Second, Allah has given people the very words with which to call on Him, words fit for His glorious Being, since people cannot choose suitable words themselves. So they are to call on Him by His attributes of perfection, without changing them.

Allah has promised to answer those who call on Him, in words quoted under 7:55 (40:60). The surest and most certain way to seek help in need and relief from distress is to call on Allah and pray for His help. It is the one way certain to succeed. Its immediate benefit is that prayer is itself an act of worship, whose reward is entered in the record of one's deeds. The Holy Prophet ﷺ said in a Tradition that calling on Allah is the essence of worship.

Allah answers supplication in many ways. Sometimes He grants the very thing asked for. At other times, when someone asks for something ill-timed or, in Allah's knowledge, unsuited to him, He gives something better or more beneficial instead. Remembering Allah by glorifying and praising Him is food for faith, īmān. It increases love, reverence and awareness of Allah, until the hardships of this world seem worthless.

### Supplications for times of distress

Al-Bukhārī, Muslim, at-Tirmidhī and an-Nasāʾī reported through authentic chains that the Holy Prophet ﷺ taught words for anyone in difficulty or grief. They begin: "There is no god but Allah, the Greatest, the Most Forbearing." They go on: "There is no god but Allah, Lord of the great Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens and the earth, Lord of the Glorious Throne."

Al-Ḥākim reported in his Mustadrak from Anas that the Holy Prophet ﷺ asked his daughter Fāṭimah al-Zahrāʾ what kept her from following his advice to say every morning and evening: "O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining, by Your mercy I seek help. Set right all my affairs, and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye." This supplication too is an effective remedy for hardship and distress.

In short, the verse gives two instructions. One is to call on Allah alone, whether seeking help or seeking to please the Creator. The other is to call on Him by His attributes of perfection, without altering them.

### What counts as abusing Allah's Names?

There are many ways of deviating from Allah's prescribed Names:

1. Calling Allah by names not found in the Holy Qur'an or the Sunnah. The scholars of the Ummah agree that it is not permissible to call Allah by names or attributes of one's own choosing, or to praise Him with names the Qur'an and Sunnah have not given. So Allah may be called Nūr, "Light", but not "white". He may be called Karīm, "Generous", but not Sakhī, though it means the same. He may be called Shāfī, "the Healer", but not Ṭabīb, "the Doctor". The matching words have the same meanings, but they are not allowed because the Qur'an and the Sunnah do not report them.
2. Avoiding a certain Name because one thinks it unsuitable in some situation. This plainly shows a lack of respect for Allah's glorious Names.
3. Giving any of Allah's beautiful Names to people. There are exceptions here. Some Names in the list are used by the Qur'an and the Sunnah for human beings, such as Raḥīm, Rashīd, ʿAlī, Karīm and ʿAzīz, and these may be used for others. Other Names denote attributes that belong to Allah alone, such as Raḥmān, Razzāq, Subḥān, Khāliq, Quddūs and Ghaffār. Using these for anyone other than Allah is forbidden in the Sharīʿah.

If someone calls a person by one of these exclusive Names out of a false belief that he has the attribute it denotes, that is unbelief. If he does so carelessly or out of ignorance, it is not unbelief. Because it resembles unbelief, though, it is a major sin.

### Why should such names not be shortened?

Sadly, many Muslims have fallen into wrong practices in naming their children and addressing people. Some have given up Islamic names altogether. Their modern names have no Islamic character, so it is hard to tell from their names that they are Muslims, especially when their appearance and manners have already lost their Islamic character. Islamic names for girls, such as Khadījah, ʿĀʾishah and Fāṭimah, have given way to fashionable names with no such character.

A sadder practice still is the careless shortening of Islamic names such as ʿAbd al-Khāliq, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, ʿAbd al-Razzāq and ʿAbd al-Quddūs to Khāliq, Raḥmān, Razzāq and Quddūs when addressing their bearers. Khāliq, the Creator, Raḥmān, the Most Merciful, Razzāq, the Provider, and Quddūs, the Most Pure, are all attributes that belong to Allah alone. Applying them to anyone else is a major sin. Each time someone addresses a person by one of them, he commits that sin again and becomes liable to great punishment.

This sinful practice has become very common among Muslims, though it brings them no gain. They fall into it only because they do not realise how grave the error is. The verse warns against it: "They will be punished for what they used to do". Many sins are committed for some worldly benefit, and the sinner may plead that necessity drove him to it. But a great many sins bring no worldly benefit at all. It is sad to see people commit them simply out of carelessness about Allah's commands and indifference to what He has forbidden or allowed. May Allah protect people from such ignorance.

### Misreading Allah

People go astray about Allah because, though they accept that He exists, they often form a wrong picture of Him. They attribute to Him things unworthy of His glory. Thinking of Him as they think of human beings, they imagine that Allah has favourites. Looking at kings, they assume He has deputies and assistants, as kings have regents and advisers. In His decisions they imagine whatever suits their own desires, though it does not accord with His justice. To attribute to Allah anything that does not befit His majesty and glory is to distort His Names.

### The inner reading: the three lamps

Allah has Names, and those Names are His attributes. Through them He is renowned, praised and recognised. They are Names full of blessing, sweet to the heart. From the pure Lord they come as pure words in a pure arrangement, and from the One Lord as beautiful words in a worthy arrangement. They are the ornament of the tongue, the lamp of the spirit and everlasting praise.

He Himself says: "My light is My guidance, 'No god but Allah' is My word, and I am He." The servant who gains access gains it through His light. When he finds the way, he finds it by His lamp: the lamp of the Sunnah, the lamp of recognition and the lamp of love. In their hearts Allah kindles the Sunnah's lamp, in their innermost selves the lamp of recognition, and in their spirits love's lamp. How happy is the servant who walks between these three lamps! Who is more exalted than one in whose heart the greatest light shines, who sees the Friend face to face in his heart? "No god but Allah" is His word and His attribute, and "Allah" is His Name. His Name tells of the One who requites and is lovingly kind, the Deity of all, the Keeper of the world, who gives the people of the world their turns.

The Pir of the Ṭarīqah had words that fit this place: "O You who alone are worthy of Your praise, O You who thank Your own giving, O You who make Your own trial sweet!" He confessed that in himself he could not praise Allah, in his intellect he could not recognise His favour, and in his ability he could not do what He deserves. "O Generous One! I am captive to the pain for which You are the cure, and slave to the praise You are worthy of. What do I know of You? You know." Allah is as He has described Himself, and what He has said of Himself, He is. This echoes the words of al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ: "I cannot count Your praises. You are as You have praised Yourself."

### In short

- Allah alone has the Most Beautiful Names, attributes of perfect excellence, and their number is not limited to ninety-nine.
- He is to be praised and called on by these Names alone, and supplication through them is the surest remedy in distress.
- Abusing His Names includes deriving idols' names from them, inventing names for Him, avoiding some of His Names, and giving His exclusive Names to people, as when names like ʿAbd al-Raḥmān are shortened.
- In the inner reading, His Names light three lamps in the servant: the Sunnah, recognition and love.

181.text:
The previous verse offered the heedless a remedy: calling on Allah by His beautiful Names. Verse 181 now speaks of those who follow the right path: "And among those We created is a group that guides with the truth and establishes justice accordingly". They guide others to the straight path and settle all their affairs as the truth, the divine law, requires.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And among those We created"**: among some of the nations Allah created.

**"is a group"**: a community that stands by the truth in word and deed. This group is the community of Muhammad ﷺ, as stated in a hadith. They are leaders of guidance whom Allah has blessed with faith and good works.

**"that guides with the truth"**: they are guided by the truth, proclaim it and call others to it so that they too may be guided.

**"and establishes justice accordingly"**: they hold to the truth themselves and judge justly by it.

### Who is this group?

It is reported that this verse refers to the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. Ibn Jarīr reported that the Holy Prophet ﷺ recited this verse and went on to say that it describes his own people. They will settle their disputes with justice and truth and be fair in all their dealings. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd reported that the Prophet ﷺ told his Companions that this verse had been revealed about them, and that before them there had been a group with the same qualities. Then he recited: "There are some among the people of Moses who guide with the truth and establish justice accordingly" (7:159). So among the Israelites there was a group with these qualities, guiding people to the truth and judging their affairs by the law of the Torah, given through Mūsā (Moses). In the same way, these qualities are the hallmark of the Muslim Ummah.

In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that a group of his Ummah will always remain openly upon the truth. Those who let them down or oppose them will not harm them, until the Hour comes. In another narration, they remain so until Allah's command arrives. In yet another, they will live in ash-Shām, Greater Syria.

### Truth and justice, then and now

The heart of the message has two parts. The first is to guide people to the right path according to the Sharīʿah. The second is to settle all disputes by the law of Islam. Together, these two qualities are the sure way to success in this world and the Hereafter. Any group or person who follows truth and justice in every area of life, and keeps personal bias out of judgement even toward enemies, belongs to the people of truth this verse describes. This was the chief mark of the Muslim Ummah. Its people kept strictly to the demands of truth and justice in all their dealings and set aside their own interests when judging between others. History records unique examples of such truthfulness in the lives of the blessed Companions and their followers.

From the day Muslims began to neglect these two qualities, decline set in plainly in every area of their life. It must be admitted, with regret, that most of the Ummah have fallen prey to their own desires. Their political, social and educational institutions are driven by petty worldly gain, and even their guidance of others is aimed mostly at worldly benefit. Many of their family ceremonies lack Islamic character and even run against the Sharīʿah. Some family customs are dressed up as religious rites, and anyone who objects to these innovations meets fierce opposition. People no longer care to organise themselves purely to spread truth and justice.

No one makes them see that this way of thinking and acting must bring disaster on the Muslims as a whole. The only way to restore the Ummah's dignity and bring it back to the path of progress and prosperity is the way of truth and justice this verse lays down. Conscious efforts should be made to awaken Muslims to these values.

### In short

- Allah has created a community that guides by the truth and judges justly by it, identified in the hadith as the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ.
- A similar group existed among the people of Mūsā, and a group of this Ummah will always stand openly on the truth until the Hour.
- Guidance by the Sharīʿah and justice in judgement are the sure path to success, and neglecting them brought the Ummah's decline.

182.text:
Verse 182 answers a question that troubles many Muslims: "As for those who deny Our signs, We will gradually draw them to destruction in ways they cannot comprehend". If progress and prosperity come only by the way of truth and justice, why do the nations far from the truth often seem more prosperous, advanced and powerful? The answer is that their prosperity is not a blessing but a respite.

### Phrase by phrase

**"As for those who deny Our signs,"** Those who deny Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an, rejecting Allah's signs without faith. These were the people of Makkah, Abū Jahl and his followers, and all who mock the punishment sent on them.

**"We will gradually draw them to destruction"** The doors of provision and livelihood will be opened for them in this life. Allah goes on providing for them, not to honour them, but to lead them on step by step until they stray even further. They are deceived by all this and say to themselves that they are on the right path.

**"in ways they cannot comprehend"**: from where they do not realise that punishment is coming. Then the punishment overtakes them when they least expect it. Allah destroyed those deniers of Makkah, each meeting a different kind of destruction.

### What is istidrāj?

Allah does not punish those who reject His signs at once for their sins. In His wisdom and mercy He lets them enjoy worldly life for a while. Then He draws them toward their disgraceful end so gradually that they do not know they are being led to it. So no one should be deceived by the present prosperity and progress of those who reject the truth. Their prosperity does them no good. It is a respite, a short period of relief before their punishment is carried out. The Qur'an calls this istidrāj, being drawn on by degrees.

Istidrāj is a severe punishment in disguise. Its essential feature is that a person is not punished for his evil deeds right away. The more evil he does, the more prosperity and possessions he is given, which keeps him from feeling guilty or heeding any warning. So he is kept from turning to Allah in repentance and saving himself from everlasting punishment. This twisted state of mind makes a person take sickness for health and poison for cure. He is left to go on with his corrupt life until death overtakes him and delivers him to eternal punishment.

### How has the Qur'an described it elsewhere?

The Holy Qur'an mentions istidrāj in many verses. One of them, quoted under 7:96 (6:44), tells how Allah poured every good thing on those who forgot His warnings, then seized them suddenly. Its sequel adds: "So the wrongdoers were utterly uprooted. And all praise is for Allah—Lord of all worlds" (6:45).

Istidrāj is not limited to disbelievers. Sinful Muslims are dealt with in the same way. That is why the righteous elders used to fear Allah when He favoured them with prosperity and comfort. They feared that their prosperity might be a sign of istidrāj.

### In short

- Allah leads those who deny His signs step by step to destruction, opening the doors of provision so that they think they are on the right path.
- Their prosperity is istidrāj, a respite before punishment that keeps them from guilt and repentance.
- Sinful Muslims can be dealt with in the same way, so the righteous feared that their comforts might be such a sign.

183.text:
Verse 183 continues the theme of istidrāj: "I ˹only˺ delay their end for a while, but My planning is flawless". The disbelievers are left to enjoy their worldly life only for a short time, and then punishment seizes them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"I ˹only˺ delay their end for a while,"** Allah gives them rein, that is to say, He prolongs the state they are in. He delays their punishment until they think it will never come. So they keep increasing in rejection and disbelief, and their punishment increases with it.

**"but My planning is flawless"**: Allah's plan is strong and perfect. His punishment and His seizing are mighty and cannot be withstood. Outwardly He shows them kindness, while intending them to be forsaken.

### Why does Allah not seize them at once?

Allah does not seize a person immediately for his wrongdoing. The delay gives him the chance either to learn from Allah's warnings and reform himself, or to grow still more fearless, so that his guilt is firmly established.

### In short

- Allah delays the punishment of the deniers for a while, giving them rein.
- The delay either lets a person reform or fixes his guilt, and Allah's plan cannot be resisted.

184.text:
Verse 184 answers the deniers' charge that the Prophet ﷺ was mad, or possessed by a jinn: "Have they not ever given it a thought? Their fellow man is not insane. He is only sent with a clear warning". A little reflection would show them that he was neither of unsound mind nor under the influence of jinn.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Have they not ever given it a thought?"** Do those who deny Allah's signs and His Messenger never think among themselves and realise the truth? Had they put their minds to work, they would have seen plainly that Muhammad ﷺ was no madman, soothsayer or sorcerer.

**"Their fellow man is not insane."** There is no trace of madness in their companion, their Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. He is not mad. He is truly the Messenger of Allah, calling them to the truth. Allah says the same elsewhere: "And your fellow man is not insane" (81:22).

**"He is only sent with a clear warning"**: he is a Messenger from Allah, sent to warn plainly of Allah's punishment, explaining things to them in a language they understand. His warning is evident to anyone with a mind and a heart that can understand and grasp it. He is only one who makes realities clear and warns of the punishment of Allah.

### How would reflection clear him?

Allah says in another verse: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I advise you to do ˹only˺ one thing: stand up for ˹the sake of˺ Allah—individually or in pairs—then reflect. Your fellow man is not insane. He is only a warner to you before ˹the coming of˺ a severe punishment.”" (34:46). The meaning is: I ask you to stand before Allah sincerely, without stubbornness or bias, alone or in groups. Then consider the man who brings you Allah's Message, and ask whether he is mad. Do that, and you will see that he is Allah's Messenger ﷺ, truly and rightly.

His matchless wisdom and knowledge are plain features of his character. Those who claim wisdom and learning are astonished that a man of such extraordinary insight and judgement could be accused of madness. To call him mad is in fact madness itself.

### When was the charge made?

Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah said it was reported that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ once stood on the hill of aṣ-Ṣafā and called out to the Quraysh, clan by clan: "O children of so-and-so, O children of so-and-so!" He warned them of Allah's might and of what He had done to His enemies. Some of them said that this companion of theirs must be mad, for he had kept shouting until morning. Then Allah sent down this verse.

### Why are men with a mission called mad?

Someone devoted to a mission lives by principle. His thinking is free of conditioning. He has risen above every kind of worldly interest, and truth becomes his only concern. He gives his life and property for a goal that seems to yield nothing in this world. That is why such a man is called crazy and out of his mind. A prophet of Allah was the greatest man with a mission of his time, so in every age people have called the prophets fanatics.

To call a missionary of Allah's religion a madman is the greatest of all transgressions. The message he brings is confirmed by all the heavens and the earth. He calls humankind to Allah, who is supremely evident in His creation throughout the universe. He tells people of the Hereafter, which weighs on the heavens and the earth like a pregnancy come to term in a woman's womb. But people do not take the truth seriously, so a man who gives his life for it seems mad to them. Had they known the real worth of truth, they would never have used the word "mad".

### In short

- The deniers called the Prophet ﷺ mad, as some of the Quraysh did after he warned them from aṣ-Ṣafā, but a little honest reflection would clear him.
- He was not insane or possessed but a clear warner, whose wisdom made the charge itself a kind of madness.
- Men devoted to a mission are often called mad by those who do not value truth, and so it was with every prophet.

185.text:
Allah challenges the deniers to look around them, and to look ahead: "Have they ever reflected on the wonders of the heavens and the earth, and everything Allah has created, and that perhaps their end is near?" Then He asks: "So what message after this ˹Quran˺ would they believe in". Verse 185 invites people to two important things. The first is thoughtful observation of Allah's creation, the heavens, the earth and everything between them. The second is mindfulness of the span of life each person has been given.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Have they ever reflected on the wonders of the heavens and the earth,"** Have the people of Makkah never considered the dominion of the heavens, with its sun, moon, stars and clouds, and the dominion of the earth, with its trees, mountains, oceans and beasts? The word malakūt means kingdom in a superlative degree, the great Kingdom. It is the same as mulk, dominion. Allah's control of the heavens and the earth holds signs. Had the deniers contemplated them and learned from them, they would be certain that the Owner of all this has no equal or rival.

**"and everything Allah has created,"** All the animals, plants and other things Allah created in them. "Everything" spells out what "what Allah has created" refers to. From all this they could infer the power of their Creator and His oneness. All of it was made by the One who alone deserves worship and sincere devotion. So they should believe in Him and in His Messenger, turn to obedience to Allah and reject every rival and idol.

**"and that perhaps their end is near?"** Have they not thought about their own lifespans, which may be close to ending, and turned to Allah in repentance while there is still time? "Perhaps" (ʿasā), when said by Allah, expresses something certain. Their destruction draws near. They should be warned that their lives may have reached their end. Then they would die as disbelievers and meet Allah's torment and severe punishment. So they should hurry to believe before they die in disbelief and move toward the Fire.

**"So what message after this ˹Quran˺ would they believe in"** If they do not believe in this Scripture, the Qur'an, with the promises and warnings it contains, what other book will they believe? Muhammad ﷺ brought them warnings and threats from Allah in His Book. If those do not move them to believe, what further warnings could?

### Why reflect on creation?

No one needs to be a genius to see the signs of Allah's power and wisdom in everything around him. A little serious thought shows that everything, indeed every particle in the world, sings the praise of its Creator. Each is in itself strong proof of Allah's power and wisdom. Anyone who uses his intellect to observe things consciously cannot escape the natural demand for faith in Allah, the One.

The deniers have not used their ordinary intelligence to seek the truth, which is evident in everything Allah has created. Allah has given them clear signs of the right path and the true faith, both within themselves and outside. For those who ignore such clear signs, nothing in the world can guide them to the right path.

### Why remember that life is short?

Awareness that one's lifespan is uncertain makes a person more active in pursuing his aims, since he cannot be sure how much time he has. All crimes and evil deeds spring from forgetting death. Those who are aware that their lifespan is uncertain mostly keep away from harmful pursuits. The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: remember often the destroyer of pleasures, death.

The deniers are not mindful that life may end at any moment. When it does, it takes away every chance to accept the truth and repent to Allah of their evil deeds.

### In short

- Allah invites people to reflect on the great kingdom of the heavens and the earth, which proves His power and oneness.
- He also reminds them that their own end may be near, a thought that keeps a person from evil.
- If they will not believe in the Qur'an, no other message will bring them to faith.

186.text:
The deniers rejected the true faith despite every clear sign Allah gave them. That could have grieved the Holy Prophet ﷺ, who cared deeply for people and wished them nothing but good. So verse 186 consoles him: "Whoever Allah allows to stray, none can guide, leaving them to wander blindly in their defiance". He had done his duty by conveying Allah's message as clearly as possible. Their rejection of the true faith was no fault of his.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Whoever Allah allows to stray,"** Whoever Allah does not guide to the truth, but sends away from the right path and from His religion. These are the people destined to be misguided.

**"none can guide,"** No one can lead them back to guidance or to His religion. Even if they try their hardest to gain guidance, it will not help them. Allah says elsewhere, of those He wills to put to fitnah, trial or error: "Whoever Allah allows to be deluded, you can never be of any help to them against Allah." (5:41). And: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Consider all that is in the heavens and the earth!” Yet neither signs nor warners are of any benefit to those who refuse to believe" (10:101).

**"leaving them to wander blindly in their defiance"** Allah leaves them in their insolence, disbelief and error, wandering blindly and hesitating in confusion. They are given up to their base desires and guided to nothing that will benefit them in the end. The verb can be read "He leaves them" or "We leave them". Read in one form, it begins a new sentence. Read in another, it joins the clause "so he has no guide".

### How do the surah's three themes fit together?

Among the themes of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, three stand out: the oneness of Allah (tawḥīd), prophethood (risālah) and the life of the Hereafter. These three principles are the mainstay of the whole edifice of Islam. The verses so far have set out the first two, tawḥīd and risālah. The next verse turns to the third.

### In short

- Verse 186 consoles the Prophet ﷺ: no one can guide those Allah leaves to stray.
- Signs and warners do not benefit those who refuse to believe, and Allah leaves them wandering in their defiance.
- The surah's three great themes are tawḥīd, prophethood and the Hereafter.

187.text:
Verse 187 turns to the third principle, the life of the Hereafter. It answers a question the deniers kept asking: "They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding the Hour, “When will it be?”" The Prophet ﷺ is told how to answer: "Say, “That knowledge is only with my Lord. He alone will reveal it when the time comes." He is to add: "It is too tremendous for the heavens and the earth and will only take you by surprise.”" Their manner of asking is exposed: "They ask you as if you had full knowledge of it." So he repeats: "Say, “That knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know.”" Allah says the same in another verse: "People ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the Hour. Say, “That knowledge is only with Allah. You never know, perhaps the Hour is near.”" (33:63).

### Phrase by phrase

**"They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding the Hour,"** Those who reject the truth in their pride, the people of Makkah, ask you, O Muhammad, about the timing of the Hour, the Resurrection. The word sāʿah means a short span of time with no fixed number of minutes or hours. In ordinary reckoning, an hour is one of the twenty-four units of a day and night. In the Qur'an, though, it names both the day when all creation will cease to exist and the day when all creation will be raised and brought before the Lord of all creation.

**"“When will it be?”"** Literally, "when is its anchoring?" Mursā means stopping or settling. Ibn ʿAbbās, as ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah reported, said they were asking when it would begin. Their question concerned the Hour's fixed term, the moment the world's end would begin.

**"Say, “That knowledge is only with my Lord."** Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ, when asked about the time of the Hour, to refer its knowledge to Allah. Only Allah knows its appointed term and when it will certainly come. No one else has that knowledge. The Prophet ﷺ was to tell them that neither he nor anyone else knows it.

**"He alone will reveal it when the time comes."** The verb comes from a root meaning to disclose or uncover. No one but Allah will make its time and occurrence manifest. "When the time comes" means at its appointed time.

**"It is too tremendous for the heavens and the earth"** Literally, "it weighs heavily in the heavens and the earth". ʿAbdur-Razzāq narrated through Maʿmar that Qatādah said its knowledge weighs on the dwellers of the heavens and the earth, since none of them knows it. Maʿmar reported that al-Ḥasan said that when it comes it will weigh heavily on them. Aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk reported that Ibn ʿAbbās said every creature will suffer its heaviness on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Jurayj said that when it begins, the heavens will be torn apart and the stars will scatter. The sun will be rolled up and lose its light, the mountains will be moved away, and all that Allah has described will happen. That is its heaviness. As-Suddī said its knowledge is hidden in the heavens and the earth. Not even an angel drawn near or a messenger sent knows its time. Others say it weighs on them because of its awesomeness, and that its coming is hidden from all in the heavens and the earth.

**"and will only take you by surprise.”"** Baghtatan means suddenly. It will come upon them all at once, while they are unaware. Qatādah said that Allah has decreed it will come only suddenly. He said it had reached them that the Prophet ﷺ described the Hour overtaking people while a man is mending his water trough, watering his cattle, laying out his goods in the market, or lowering and raising his scales.

**"They ask you as if you had full knowledge of it."** The word used is ḥafiyy. Ibn ʿAbbās said it means a scholar or someone well informed. It is generally used for a person who spends his effort and all his resources to find something out. The sound explanation, narrated from Mujāhid through Ibn Abī Najīḥ, is: as if you had asked about its time, so that you now know it. Others render it: as if you were preoccupied with asking about it until you came to know it, or as if you were eager to know it.
