They did not realise that he did not ask about it because he knew his Lord. One explanation adds other meanings: as if you were ignorant of it, or as if you had forgotten it.

Al-ʿAwfī reported Ibn ʿAbbās explaining it as: as if you were on friendly terms with them! When the pagans of Quraysh asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour, they asked as though he were their close friend. Allah then revealed that He alone holds this knowledge and has shared it with no messenger and no angel near Him.

**"Say, “That knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know.”"** "Only" is for emphasis. Most people, the people of Makkah, do not know that its knowledge lies with Allah alone, and they do not believe in it.

### Why was the question asked?

It is said that the verse came down about the Quraysh or about the Jews. It seems to concern the Quraysh, since the verse was revealed in Makkah. The Quraysh used to ask about the Hour because they denied it and dismissed its coming. Allah says: "They ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass if what you say is true?”" (10:48). And: "Those who disbelieve in it ˹ask to˺ hasten it ˹mockingly˺. But the believers are fearful of it, knowing that it is the truth. Surely those who dispute about the Hour have gone far astray" (42:18).

Ibn Jarīr and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd reported from Qatādah that the Quraysh of Makkah once asked the Holy Prophet ﷺ, mockingly, when the Hour he so often warned them of would come. The verse was revealed in answer. In another report from Qatādah, the Quraysh told him that there were ties of kinship between them, so he should tell them the Hour's timing. Ibn ʿAbbās said that two Jews, Jabal ibn Qushayr and Shamwāl ibn Zayd, told him to say when the Hour would be if he really was a prophet, since they claimed to know it. Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept speaking of the Hour, because people kept asking about it, until this verse was revealed. An-Nasāʾī collected this report, which has a strong chain.

### Why is its time kept secret?

The heart of the verse is the answer the Quraysh of Makkah were to receive. The exact time of the Hour is not known and will never be made known to anyone. It is a divine secret that will reveal itself by happening suddenly, as the words "will only take you by surprise" decree. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim reported from Abū Hurayrah that the Holy Prophet ﷺ spoke of the sudden coming of the Qiyāmah, the Day of Resurrection, saying that it has been kept a close secret.

The wisdom of this is plain. It lets people live their lives in peace, which would be impossible if they knew the exact time of their death. Besides, those who deny the Last Day would mock it all the more if they knew it lay far in the future. Divine wisdom chose to leave it undefined, so that people stay in a general fear of its terrors. That fear is an effective check on crime and corruption.

Once a person believes that the Day of Resurrection must come, that all creation will stand before the Lord of all creation, and that every deed, small or great, will be rewarded or punished, the time of its coming no longer matters. It is unwise to waste precious hours on idle debates about when the Last Day will come. Reason and wisdom demand instead that every moment of an uncertain life be spent carefully in preparing for the great Day of Judgement. This answer showed the Quraysh of Makkah that their question about its time came from ignorance.

Questions like "On what day will the Last Day come?" come from minds that are not serious. The sincere believe in the Day of Judgement without wanting to know its date. Since this world is a place of testing, the Last Day can be spoken of here only as a caution and a warning.

### Did the Prophet ﷺ know, and hide it?

The words "They ask you as if you had full knowledge of it" expose another misconception of the disbelievers of Makkah. They thought the Holy Prophet ﷺ had somehow learned the exact time of the Last Day and was keeping it back for some reason, and they pressed him to reveal it. He was told to answer that its knowledge is with Allah alone, though most people do not know.

A prophet need not know the exact time of the Last Day, or certain other matters Allah keeps secret. A prophet's lack of knowledge in such matters is no argument against his prophethood. A prophet's knowledge can never equal Allah's all-embracing knowledge.

### The questioner who knew no less

Jibrīl (Gabriel) once came in the form of a bedouin to teach people their religion. He sat beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and questioned him as if to learn. He asked about Islām, then about īmān, faith, then about iḥsān, excellence in religion. Then he asked when the Hour would come. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied that the one being asked knew no more about it than the one asking. He meant that he knew no more about it than Jibrīl, and that no one knows more about it than anyone else. Then the Prophet ﷺ recited: "Indeed, Allah ˹alone˺ has the knowledge of the Hour." (31:34).

In another narration, Jibrīl asked about the signs of the Hour, and the Prophet ﷺ described them. He also said that five things are known only to Allah, and recited the same verse (31:34). After each answer, Jibrīl would say, "You have spoken the truth." The Companions wondered at a questioner who asked a question and then confirmed every answer. When Jibrīl left, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told the Companions that this was Jibrīl, who had come to teach them their religion. In yet another narration, the Prophet ﷺ said he had recognised Jibrīl in every form in which he came to him, except this one.

### "Your Hour" and the hundred years

Muslim recorded from ʿĀʾishah that when bedouins came to the Prophet ﷺ, they would ask him about the Hour. He would point to the youngest among them and say that if this one lived, he would not grow old before their Hour came. He meant the end of their own lives, which brings them into the barzakh, the realm between this life and the Hereafter. Muslim also recorded from Anas that a man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Hour. He answered that if this young boy lived, perhaps he would not grow old before the Hour came. Only Muslim collected this hadith.

Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh said he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, a month before he died, that people kept asking him about the Hour though its knowledge is with Allah. He swore by Allah that not one soul then living on the earth would be alive a hundred years later. Muslim collected this hadith. A similar hadith is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from Ibn ʿUmar, who explained that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ meant that his generation would have come to its end by then.

### What did the greatest prophets know?

Imām Aḥmad recorded from Ibn Masʿūd that the Prophet ﷺ said that on the night of the Isrāʾ he met Ibrāhīm (Abraham), Mūsā (Moses) and ʿĪsā (Jesus). They spoke of the Hour and asked Ibrāhīm about it, but he said he had no knowledge of it. They asked Mūsā, who also said he did not know. Then they asked ʿĪsā. He said that only Allah, the Exalted and Most Honoured, knows when it will come. But his Lord had told him that the Dajjāl, the False Messiah, would appear, and that ʿĪsā would have two staffs with him. When the Dajjāl saw him, he would melt as lead melts, and Allah would destroy him. Even tree and stone would call out to the Muslim that a disbeliever was hiding behind it, and tell him to come and kill him. Allah would destroy the Dajjāl and his army, and people would return safely to their lands.

After that, ʿĪsā said, Gog and Magog would come swarming from every height, overrunning the earth and destroying all they passed. They would drink dry every water source in their path. People would come to him complaining of them. He would call on Allah against them, and Allah would bring death to them all, until the earth reeked with their stench. Then Allah would send rain to wash their corpses into the sea. His Lord had told him that when this happens, the Hour will be like a woman whose pregnancy has reached full term. Her family cannot tell when she will surprise them with the birth, by night or by day. Ibn Mājah collected a similar hadith.

These were the greatest of the messengers, yet they did not know the Hour's appointed time. When they asked ʿĪsā, he spoke only of its signs, because he will descend in the last generations of this Ummah. He will rule by the Law of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, kill the Dajjāl and destroy Gog and Magog through the blessing of his supplication. ʿĪsā simply told them what knowledge Allah had given him on the matter.

### Trials and harj before the Hour

Imām Aḥmad recorded from Ḥudhayfah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the Hour. He said that its knowledge is with his Lord, the Exalted and Most Honoured, and no one but He will reveal its time. But he would tell them of its signs and what comes before it: there would be fitnah, trials, and harj. They said they knew what fitnah meant, but asked what harj was. He said it means killing, in the language of the Ethiopians. Then he added that people would become so isolated and estranged that hardly anyone would recognise anyone else. None of the six collections has this hadith through this chain.

Abū Mūsā said the same, speaking on a Friday from the pulpit of the main mosque of Baṣrah. He had been present when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the time of the Hour. He answered that no one but Allah knows it, and that He alone will reveal it at its time. But he would tell them of its signs and what would precede it: there would be a lot of trials and harj. Asked what harj meant, he said it is an Abyssinian word meaning killing. He also described hearts growing dry, and people cast among strangers so that they hardly know one another. Those of sound mind would pass away, and only a weak people would remain, who neither recognise good nor forbid evil.

### The Prophet ﷺ who came close to the Hour

The Holy Prophet ﷺ was, however, given knowledge of certain specific signs showing that the Last Day was near, and he told the Muslim Ummah of them plainly in his Traditions. He is the unlettered Prophet, the chief and seal of the messengers, Muhammad ﷺ. He is the Prophet of mercy and the Prophet of repentance. He is also the Prophet of al-Malḥamah, the great battle against the disbelievers, and al-ʿĀqib, who came after many prophets. He is al-Muqaffī, the last in their succession, and al-Ḥāshir, at whose feet all people will be gathered. As recorded in the Ṣaḥīḥ from Anas and Sahl ibn Saʿd, and also by at-Tirmidhī, he said that his sending and the Hour are as close as these two, joining his index and middle fingers. Yet even he was commanded, when asked about the Hour, to leave its knowledge to Allah.

### How old is the world?

Reports that give the world a total age of seven thousand years were borrowed from Israelite literature into certain Islamic books. They are not authentic and have no basis in the Qur'an or the Sunnah. Likewise, modern geophysical findings that put the world's age at millions of years conflict neither with the Qur'an nor with any sound Tradition of the Holy Prophet ﷺ.

On the contrary, the Holy Prophet ﷺ told the Muslim Ummah in a Tradition that, compared with the peoples before them, they were like a single white hair on the body of a black ox. This gives some idea of how vast the world's age is. Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥazm of Spain therefore concluded that no one can calculate the exact age of the world. It seems impossible in any case to work out the exact age of the universe. Doing so would reveal exactly when it will end, and the verse rules that out, since only Allah knows when the Last Day will come.

### In short

- The deniers of Makkah asked mockingly when the Hour would come, and the Prophet ﷺ was told to answer that only Allah knows.
- It weighs on the heavens and the earth, and it will come suddenly, amid people's everyday business.
- Not even Jibrīl or the greatest prophets knew its time, though the Prophet ﷺ was shown its signs, such as trials and killing.
- Its time is hidden so that people live in peace yet stay in awe of it, and the wise spend their lives preparing for it, not asking its date.

188.text:
Verse 188 clears away a common misbelief about Allah's prophets: "Say, “I have no power to benefit or protect myself, except by the Will of Allah." The Prophet ﷺ goes on: "If I had known the unknown, I would have benefited myself enormously, and no harm would have ever touched me." He states what he is: "I am only a warner and deliverer of good news for those who believe.”" People imagined that prophets must know everything in the universe, including the unseen future and the unknown past. They also thought prophets could bring benefit or harm to anyone by their own will. The verse makes clear that all-embracing knowledge is an attribute of Allah alone and cannot be ascribed to any creature.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, “I have no power to benefit or protect myself,"** Say, O Muhammad, to the people of Makkah: I cannot bring good to myself or ward off harm from myself. Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to entrust all matters to Him.

**"except by the Will of Allah."** Except whatever benefit or harm Allah wills for me. The control of these things belongs to Allah alone. The Prophet ﷺ was told to say that he does not know the unseen future, and knows of it only what Allah tells him. Allah says in another verse: "˹He is the˺ Knower of the unseen, disclosing none of it to anyone" (72:26).

**"If I had known the unknown,"** If I had knowledge of the ghayb, the unseen, of benefit and harm and of what is hidden from me.

**"I would have benefited myself enormously,"** Aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk reported that Ibn ʿAbbās said this refers to wealth. In another narration Ibn ʿAbbās explained: I would know how much profit I would make on what I bought, and I would always sell at a profit. Ibn Jarīr said that others explained: if I knew the unseen, I would store up in the good years for the years of famine, and prepare in advance for times of high prices. One explanation says: if I knew when I would die, I would do good and righteous deeds in abundance. Another says: if I knew when punishment would fall on you, I would do much good out of gratitude, and grief for you would not touch me.

**"and no harm would have ever touched me."** Poverty would never have touched me, Ibn ʿAbbās said. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam explained: I would have avoided every kind of harm and protected myself from it before it came. Knowing things before they happened, I would have taken precautions against poverty and every other hardship.

**"I am only a warner and deliverer of good news for those who believe.”"** I am only a Messenger from Allah. I warn the disbelievers of the Fire and its painful punishment, and I bring the righteous good news of Paradise and Allah's generous reward. This is for people who believe in Paradise and Hell, who believe that he is Allah's Messenger, and who believe in what was revealed to him. As Allah says: "Indeed, We have made this ˹Quran˺ easy in your own language ˹O Prophet˺ so with it you may give good news to the righteous and warn those who are contentious" (19:97).

### Why was the verse revealed?

Al-Kalbī said that the people of Makkah asked the Prophet ﷺ whether his Lord did not tell him when prices were low before they rose, so that he could buy and make a profit. They also asked whether He did not tell him which land was about to suffer drought, so that he could move to more fertile land. Allah then revealed this verse.

### Did the Prophet ﷺ know the unseen?

Ascribing Allah's exclusive attributes to anyone else is the greatest transgression and amounts to setting up partners with Allah. The very purpose of the Qur'an's revelation and of the Holy Prophet's coming ﷺ was to remove every trace of plural gods and establish the purest tawḥīd, the oneness of Allah. So the Holy Prophet ﷺ was told to declare that, quite apart from others, he could not even harm or benefit himself, and that he did not have knowledge of the unseen. Had he had such knowledge, he would have gathered every good for himself and saved himself from every possible harm.

There are clear instances when the Holy Prophet ﷺ could not achieve his aims despite all his efforts, and many others when he could not protect himself from harm. The treaty of Ḥudaybiyah is one clear example. Intending ʿUmrah, the Holy Prophet ﷺ made the long journey to Makkah with his Companions, only to be stopped by its unbelievers. Despite all their longing and effort, they had to return to Madinah without performing the ʿUmrah. Likewise, the Holy Prophet ﷺ was wounded at the battle of Uḥud, and the Muslims suffered a temporary defeat.

Perhaps such events were allowed to happen to show in practice that the prophets, though closest to Allah and the best of all people, did not have divine power or all-embracing knowledge. They were human beings like others. The Christians fell into exactly this error, ascribing Allah's divine attributes to their Prophet, and went astray.

### What knowledge were the prophets given?

Allah does give the prophets more knowledge and power than any other human being has ever had. The Holy Prophet ﷺ was certainly granted knowledge beyond that of all the other prophets. He told the Muslims of many things that would happen in the future, and every one of his predictions came true exactly as he foretold.

So it is right to say that the Holy Prophet ﷺ was given knowledge of a number of unseen things. In the Qur'an's terms, however, this is not called "knowledge of the unseen" (ʿilm al-ghayb). For this reason it is not permissible to call the Holy Prophet ﷺ "the Knower of the unseen", since no one but Allah is the Knower of the unseen. His assigned duty is to warn evildoers of Allah's punishment and to give the righteous the good news of Allah's great reward.

### In short

- The Prophet ﷺ was told to declare that he had no power to benefit or protect himself except as Allah willed, and no knowledge of the unseen.
- Had he known the unseen, he would have gathered wealth and avoided all harm, yet he was turned back at Ḥudaybiyah and wounded at Uḥud.
- All-embracing knowledge belongs to Allah alone, and ascribing it to any creature is a form of setting up partners with Him.
- The Prophet ﷺ was given knowledge of many unseen things, but he is not called "the Knower of the unseen". His role is to warn and give good news.

189.text:
Verse 189 turns to the most basic belief of Islam, tawḥīd, and at the same time shows the falsehood of believing in more than one god. It begins with the creation of Adam and Ḥawwāʾ (Eve), a display of Allah's perfect power: "He is the One Who created you from a single soul, then from it made its spouse so he may find comfort in her." It goes on to the birth of a child: "After he had been united with her, she carried a light burden that developed gradually." Then comes the anxious prayer: "When it grew heavy, they prayed to Allah, their Lord, “If you grant us good offspring, we will certainly be grateful.”" Such a display of Allah's power should have made people more grateful to Him and kept them from setting up partners with Him. Being heedless, they did otherwise, as this verse and the next describe.

### Phrase by phrase

**"He is the One Who created you from a single soul,"** Allah created all humankind from Adam alone, and from Adam He created his wife Ḥawwāʾ. From the two of them people spread. Allah says elsewhere: "O humanity! Indeed, We created you from a male and a female, and made you into peoples and tribes so that you may ˹get to˺ know one another. Surely the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous among you." (49:13). The most noble is the one with the most taqwā. And: "O humanity! Be mindful of your Lord Who created you from a single soul, and from it He created its mate" (4:1).

**"then from it made its spouse so he may find comfort in her."** Allah created Adam's wife, Eve, from his rib, so that he would be close to her, find rest and peace with her, and be intimate and tender with her. Allah says in another verse: "And one of His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves so that you may find comfort in them. And He has placed between you compassion and mercy." (30:21). No two souls are as intimate as husband and wife. That is why Allah mentions that a sorcerer may use his tricks to separate a man from his wife, which shows how hard they are to part in normal circumstances.

**"After he had been united with her,"** Literally, "when he covered her", meaning when he had marital relations with her.

**"she carried a light burden"** This is the first stage of pregnancy, when the woman feels no pain and may not even notice it. The foetus is then only a nuṭfah, a mixed drop, then an ʿalaqah, a clinging clot, then a muḍghah, a small lump of flesh. Maymūn ibn Mihrān reported that his father said she found the pregnancy unnoticeable.

**"that developed gradually."** Literally, "and she went about with it". Mujāhid said it means she continued with the pregnancy, and the same is reported from al-Ḥasan, Ibrāhīm an-Nakhaʿī and as-Suddī. Ayyūb asked al-Ḥasan about this phrase. Al-Ḥasan replied that had Ayyūb been an Arab he would know: it means she carried the pregnancy on through its stages. Qatādah said it means it became clear that she was pregnant. Ibn Jarīr explained that the fluid stayed in her whether she stood or sat. Al-ʿAwfī recorded that Ibn ʿAbbās said the seed remained, but she was unsure whether she had conceived. Others say she came and went easily because the burden was light, going about her affairs without finding it heavy.

**"When it grew heavy,"** As the child grew in her womb, she became heavier with it, as as-Suddī explained.

**"they prayed to Allah, their Lord,"** They grew anxious about the child. Ibn ʿAbbās, as aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk reported, said they feared it might be born in the shape of an animal. Abū al-Bakhtarī and Abū Mālik said they feared it might not be human. One explanation says Satan's whispering made them think it was a beast. Another says they feared it would be born unable to speak.

**"“If you grant us good offspring, we will certainly be grateful.”"** They asked for a child sound and whole, a human being in every respect, and promised to be grateful for it. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said it means: if You give us a boy.

### How do parents fall into shirk?

At the start of a pregnancy the woman moves about freely. Later, as the foetus grows heavy in her womb, the parents worry about their unborn child. They cannot be sure the child will be whole, since sometimes a newborn is not normal, or is deaf, dumb or blind. In their worry they pray for a healthy child and promise Allah they will be grateful if He grants one. Then, when Allah answers their prayer with a normal, healthy baby, they set up partners with Him. So their own children become the cause of their going astray.

This happens in many ways. Some are misled by the false belief that their newborn is the gift of some holy or godly person. Some dedicate the child to a living or dead person and begin making offerings in that person's name. Some take their children to such people and bow their foreheads before them. Some fall into shirk by naming their children ʿAbd al-Lāt, ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, ʿAbd al-Shams or Bandah ʿAlī, and the like. Such names assign the children to false gods, as though those gods or persons had created or given them.

### Man and woman, a sign of the One Creator

This vast universe itself introduces its Creator, and the way it does so leaves no room for polytheism. The universe holds countless separate things, yet all of them combine into one harmonious whole, with no contradiction or clash among them. Such perfect harmony would be impossible unless the Creator and Lord of the universe were One, controlling all its workings.

Consider man and woman. Each is born an independent being, yet the two complete each other in every sense. The harmony is so perfect that each feels created for the other. This is one of the most wonderful examples of harmony in the world. It is clear proof that male and female were created by one and the same Lord. Had more than one being been at work in the universe, such perfect harmony between two different and opposite beings could not exist.

### The inner reading: wonders from a single drop

Great and magnificent is the lovingly kind Lord, beautiful in name, Keeper of His servants, Creator of all people, Caretaker of all! He is pure and faultless in name and sign. He has no offspring and was not born, and He has no partner or helper, no spouse and no likeness. When He created the creatures, He made them in pairs, linked to one another. He joined male and female, matched like to like and kind to kind, as He says: "and made of it its spouse, so that it may rest in her". He is Allah, the One, peerless in His attributes and free of every fault, the Creator, Keeper and Nurturer.

When He wishes to show His power in creation, He brings a hundred thousand subtleties and wonders out of one drop of feeble water. First there is dust, then water, then a clot, then tissue, then bones and skin, and then a living creature. At four months it comes to life, held "in a secure place" (77:21), within "three layers of darkness" (39:6). In each person He made three pools: the brain, the liver and the heart. From the brain, the streams of the nerves branch through the whole body, carrying the power of sensation and movement. From the liver the veins spread throughout the body to carry nourishment. From the heart the arteries spread throughout it to carry the spirit.

He made the brain in three layers, placing understanding in the first, intellect in the second and memory in the third. He made the eye in seven layers and set brightness and sight within them. More wondrous still is the pupil. It is the size of a single lentil, yet the whole vast form of heaven and earth appears within it. More surprising yet is the forehead, made firm and hard so that it grows no hair to spoil its beauty. Within it He made the skin of the eyebrow, so that a little hair grows there, but never too long.

### In short

- Allah created all humankind from Adam, and from him his wife, so that spouses would find comfort, love and mercy in each other.
- The verse traces a pregnancy from its light beginning to the parents' anxious prayer for a sound child, with their promise of gratitude.
- Many parents, once granted a healthy child, fall into shirk by crediting holy persons or naming the child after false gods.
- The perfect harmony of man and woman, and the wonders formed from one drop, point to the One Creator.

190.text:
The promise of gratitude was broken: "But when He granted their descendants good offspring, they associated false gods in what He has given them. Exalted is Allah above what they associate ˹with Him˺". All these acts and beliefs are forms of shirk and the worst kind of ingratitude to Allah, their Lord. The verse's last sentence confirms that such people have gone astray.

### Phrase by phrase

**"But when He granted their descendants good offspring,"** When Allah answered their prayer and gave them a healthy child, a sound human being, as they had asked.

**"they associated false gods in what He has given them."** A variant reading has "a partner" in place of "partners". One account says they made Iblīs a partner in naming the child, calling him ʿAbdullāh and ʿAbd al-Ḥārith. The name ʿAbd al-Ḥārith means "servant of al-Ḥārith", though no one should be called the servant of anyone but Allah, as in ʿAbd Allāh.

**"Exalted is Allah above what they associate ˹with Him˺"** Allah is far above having any partner, and He alone is divine. He is free of the idols the people of Makkah associate with Him. Grammatically, this sentence follows on from "He is the One Who created you", so what lies between the two is a parenthesis.

### Who set up the partners?

Ibn Jarīr recorded that al-Ḥasan said this was done by the followers of some religion, not by Adam. Al-Ḥasan also said the verse refers to those of Adam's offspring who fell into shirk. Qatādah said al-Ḥasan used to say it refers to the Jews and the Christians. Allah gave them children, and they made them Jews and Christians.

These explanations go back to al-Ḥasan through authentic chains, and this is one of the best interpretations. The verse should be understood this way. It plainly does not refer to Adam and Ḥawwāʾ but to the idolaters among their offspring. Allah mentioned the individuals first, Adam and Ḥawwāʾ, and then moved on to the species, humankind, many of whom fell into shirk. The Qur'an has similar cases. For example: "And indeed, We adorned the lowest heaven with ˹stars like˺ lamps, and made them ˹as missiles˺ for stoning ˹eavesdropping˺ devils" (67:5). The stars that serve as lamps in the sky are well known not to be the same as the missiles hurled at the devils. Allah knows best.

On this reading, Adam and Ḥawwāʾ are mentioned at the start so that their children may follow them and be grateful to Allah. The rest of the passage speaks of the misguidance of their descendants, who set up partners with their Lord instead of thanking Him. So Adam and Ḥawwāʾ have nothing to do with those who committed shirk. This interpretation rests on Ibn ʿAbbās, as Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported, and as recorded in al-Durr al-Manthūr.

### The report about the name ʿAbd al-Ḥārith

Mujāhid said that at first all the children of Adam and Eve died in infancy. Satan whispered to them that if a boy was born they should name him ʿAbd al-Ḥārith, al-Ḥārith having been Satan's name before. They did so, and this is the meaning of "they associated false gods in what He has given them". Samurah ibn Jundub reported a hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ said that when Eve gave birth, none of her children survived. Satan came to her and told her to name the child ʿAbd al-Ḥārith so that it would live. She did, and it lived. This came from Satan's prompting and his doing. Al-Ḥākim reported this hadith and graded it ṣaḥīḥ, and al-Tirmidhī reported it and graded it ḥasan gharīb.

Some scholars regard this story, related by at-Tirmidhī and al-Ḥākim, of Adam and Ḥawwāʾ being deceived by Satan, as an unauthentic Israelite report to be rejected. Many scholars of hadith, on the other hand, have confirmed it. Even if the story is taken as authentic, it does not mean Adam associated a partner with Allah in worship, since Adam was protected from such a sin. The interpretation above removes any possible doubt in either case.

### What do these two verses teach?

1. Men and women were created as one species so that they would share a natural affinity and full understanding, and fulfil their duties in building a good society.
2. The rights and duties given to husband and wife are meant above all to make the home peaceful. Many social habits of the modern age run directly against this aim. What is called the freedom of women, in the sense of free mixing between men and women, has wrought havoc on social peace. The alarming number of divorces and bitter quarrels mostly stems from it. Experience shows that as immodest practices grow in a society, its social values decay in proportion, robbing people of peace at home and in society.
3. It is forbidden to give children names such as ʿAbd al-Shams, "slave of the Sun", or ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, "slave of al-ʿUzzā", which assign them to anyone other than Allah. Such names are forbidden even if the parents do not really mean it, and giving them is a great sin in Islam.
4. The best way to thank Allah is to name one's children after the beautiful Names of Allah and the names of His Messenger. The Holy Prophet ﷺ recommended names like ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿAbdullāh.

Sadly, Muslims are giving up their Islamic manners and values one by one. Many give their children non-Islamic names simply to follow the fashion of other cultures. Many parents also shorten their children's names to English initials, which makes them even harder to recognise as Muslims, especially once Muslims have taken on the appearance of others entirely. May Allah grant Muslims a true understanding of Islam and its values.

### In short

- Granted a healthy child, people broke their promise of gratitude and set up partners with Allah in what He had given them.
- Al-Ḥasan's interpretation, with authentic chains and also supported by Ibn ʿAbbās, applies this to Adam's idolatrous descendants, not to Adam and Ḥawwāʾ.
- A report that Satan had them name a child ʿAbd al-Ḥārith is graded sound by some and rejected by others. Even if true, it was no shirk in worship.
- Children should not be given names that make them servants of anyone but Allah.

191.text:
Allah now rebukes the idolaters directly: "Do they associate ˹with Allah˺ those ˹idols˺ which cannot create anything, but are in fact created". Allah reproaches those who worshipped idols, rivals and images besides Him. Allah created these objects, and they own nothing and can bring neither harm nor benefit. They cannot see, and they cannot help those who worship them. They are lifeless things that neither move, hear nor see. Their worshippers are better than they are, since the worshippers can hear and see and have strength of their own.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Do they associate ˹with Allah˺ those ˹idols˺ which cannot create anything,"** Do you set up as partners with Allah things that neither create nor have any power to create, nor to give life? They know that these idols create nothing, so how can they count them as Allah's partners in divinity, worthy of worship?

**"but are in fact created"** These worshipped objects were themselves created and made. They are created in the sense that they were carved. As Ibrāhīm al-Khalīl, the Friend of Allah, said to his people: "How can you worship what you carve ˹with your own hands˺" (37:95).

### Could they create even a fly?

Allah says in another verse: "O humanity! A lesson is set forth, so listen to it ˹carefully˺: those ˹idols˺ you invoke besides Allah can never create ˹so much as˺ a fly, even if they ˹all˺ were to come together for that. And if a fly were to snatch anything away from them, they cannot ˹even˺ retrieve it from the fly. How powerless are those who invoke and those invoked. They have not shown Allah the reverence He deserves. Surely Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty" (22:73-74).

Even if all the disbelievers' false gods joined their strength, they could not create a fly. If a fly stole the smallest thing from them and flew off, they could not get it back. If a thing is that weak, how can it be worshipped and called on for provision and help?

### In short

- Allah rebukes those who give Him partners that cannot create anything and were themselves carved and made.
- All their false gods together could not create a fly, or recover what a fly took from them.
- Their worshippers, who can hear, see and act, are better than the idols they worship.

192.text:
The idols are as helpless as they are lifeless: "which cannot help them, or even help themselves". They cannot help their worshippers, and they cannot even defend themselves.

### Phrase by phrase

**"which cannot help them,"** They cannot give victory to those who worship them or save them from defeat.

**"or even help themselves"** They cannot protect themselves against anyone who means to harm them, whether by breaking them or in any other way. They cannot stop what is done to them. The question in the previous verse is a rebuke. Since such things cannot help those who worship them, or even themselves, worshipping them is plainly foolish and ignorant.

### Idols that could not defend themselves

Ibrāhīm al-Khalīl, the Friend of Allah, broke and disgraced the idols of his people, as Allah describes: "Then he swiftly turned on them, striking ˹them˺ with his right hand" (37:93). And: "So he smashed them into pieces, except the biggest of them, so they might turn to it ˹for answers˺" (21:58).

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to al-Madinah, Muʿādh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ and Muʿādh ibn Jabal accepted Islam while they were still young. At night they used to raid the idolaters' idols. They broke and defaced them and used them as firewood for needy widows, hoping to teach their people a lesson and show them their error.

Among his people's chiefs was ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ, who kept an idol that he worshipped and anointed with perfume. The two Muʿādhs used to go to it, turn it upside down and smear it with animal dung. When ʿAmr saw what had happened, he would clean his idol, perfume it and leave a sword beside it, telling it to defend itself. The young men repeated their prank, and he repeated his care. In the end they bound the idol to a dead dog with a rope and dropped it into a well.

When ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ saw this, he knew his religion was false. He swore by Allah that if it had been a god with any power, it would not have ended up tied to a dog on a rope. ʿAmr accepted Islam and was firm in it. He was later martyred at the battle of Uḥud. May Allah be pleased with him and make Paradise his home.

### In short

- The idols cannot help their worshippers, nor even defend themselves.
- Ibrāhīm smashed his people's idols, and none of them could resist.
- When two young Companions disgraced ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ's idol, he saw it was powerless, accepted Islam and died a martyr at Uḥud.

193.text:
The idols cannot even hear a call: "And if you ˹idolaters˺ call upon them for guidance, they cannot respond to you. It is all the same whether you call them or remain silent". They are mere objects without awareness. They do not hear and cannot speak.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And if you ˹idolaters˺ call upon them for guidance, they cannot respond to you."** If you call these idols, which you have taken as gods, to guidance, they will not follow you or answer what you call them to. The verb can be read yatbaʿūkum or yattabiʿūkum. Allah says elsewhere: "If you call upon them, they cannot hear your calls. And if they were to hear, they could not respond to you." (35:14).

One explanation offers a second reading. The address is to the Prophet ﷺ: if you call the disbelievers to guidance, to Allah's oneness, they will not follow you. On the first reading, the disbelievers are addressed: the idols will give no answer when called to the truth, since they are dead things, not living.

**"It is all the same whether you call them or remain silent"** The idols do not hear those who worship them, so the result is the same whether they call on them or shun them. The idols will not follow, because they cannot hear. On the second reading, the disbelievers will not follow the Prophet ﷺ in Allah's oneness, whether he calls them or keeps silent.

### What did Ibrāhīm ask his father?

Ibrāhīm said: "O dear father! Why do you worship what can neither hear nor see, nor benefit you at all" (19:42). The idols hear no call and see no one, so they can give no guidance and bring no benefit. A thing that cannot respond to a call is no more use when called than when left alone.

### In short

- The idols cannot answer any call, for they are lifeless objects that neither hear nor speak.
- Calling them or keeping silent makes no difference, as Ibrāhīm told his father.
- On another reading, the stubborn disbelievers will not follow the Prophet's call to Allah's oneness, whether he calls them or not.

194.text:
The Prophet ﷺ is told to say to the idolaters what their gods really are: "Those ˹idols˺ you invoke besides Allah are created beings like yourselves." Then comes a challenge: "So call upon them and see if they will answer you, if your claims are true". The idols, like those who worship them, were created.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Those ˹idols˺ you invoke besides Allah"**: the idols you call on and worship instead of Allah.

**"are created beings like yourselves."** Literally, "servants like you". Allah created them and they belong to Him, so in that respect they are the same as their worshippers, servants He owns. Yet the people are better than the idols, since they are alive, can speak and walk, hear and see, and can do harm. The idols have no such powers. The false gods are mere servants like their worshippers. Lacking the basic faculties of moving, seeing, hearing and speaking, they cannot help themselves, let alone help others in need.

**"So call upon them and see if they will answer you, if your claims are true"** Call on the idols, then, and let them hear your call and answer it, if you are telling the truth when you claim they are gods who can benefit you. Allah then goes on to show how utterly helpless they are, and how far their worshippers surpass them.

### In short

- The idols are created and owned by Allah, just like the people who worship them.
- Their worshippers can move, see, hear and speak, so they are better than their idols.
- The idolaters are challenged to call on their gods and see whether they answer.

195.text:
Allah now shows how helpless the idols are, and how far their worshippers surpass them: "Do they have feet to walk with? Or hands to hold with? Or eyes to see with? Or ears to hear with?" Then the Prophet ﷺ throws down a challenge: "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Call upon your associate-gods and conspire against me without delay". The questions deny that the idols have any of these things. The idolaters have them all, so why worship what is less complete than themselves?

### Phrase by phrase

**"Do they have feet to walk with?"** Can they walk toward any good? The question is a denial: they have no feet.

**"Or hands to hold with?"** Hands with which to give and take, to act or to strike. The word for hands, aydin, is the plural of yad.

**"Or eyes to see with?"** Can they see your worship of them?

**"Or ears to hear with?"** Can they hear your call? If these idols can do none of these things, how can you worship them, hoping they will bring you benefit or protect you from harm?

**"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Call upon your associate-gods"** Say, O Muhammad, to the idolaters of Makkah: call on all your partners together and seek your gods' help against me.

**"and conspire against me without delay"** Plot against me all together, do whatever you will to destroy me, and give me no respite, not even for a moment. Put all your effort into it, for I am not concerned with you.

### Who made the same challenge before?

Hūd (Hud) answered his people in the same way. They told him: "All we can say is that some of our gods have possessed you with evil.” He said, “I call Allah to witness, and you too bear witness, that I ˹totally˺ reject whatever you associate with Him ˹in worship˺. So let all of you plot against me without delay. I have put my trust in Allah—my Lord and your Lord. There is no living creature that is not completely under His control. Surely my Lord’s Way is perfect justice" (11:54-56).

### Why do people worship what cannot walk or see?

It is astonishing that, in a world with so many arguments for one Lord, people make polytheism their religion. Through the wonderful harmony between two human beings, a child is born. Some then believe this happened through the blessing of some living or dead saint. Some credit it to imagined deities. Some say it came from the blind interplay of material forces. Others think the beautiful baby was the reward of their own efforts.

Behind the idols of stone or metal that polytheists set up lies a "philosophy". The idols are said to be outward forms in which the god they stand for has become incarnate, so worshipping them amounts to worshipping that god. Among ordinary people, though, polytheism takes the form of regarding the idols themselves as holy. These idols cannot walk, talk, see or hear. Yet superstitious people imagine that they will be of use to them and meet their needs.

### In short

- The idols have no feet, hands, eyes or ears, so their worshippers are more complete than they are.
- The Prophet ﷺ challenged the idolaters to call on all their gods and plot against him at once, as Hūd challenged his people.
- People credit a child's birth to saints, deities, blind forces or themselves, and treat helpless idols as holy.

196.text:
The Prophet ﷺ explains why he does not fear them: "“Indeed, my Protector is Allah Who has revealed this Book. For He ˹alone˺ protects the righteous". Verse 196 gives the ground of his confidence. Allah, who revealed the Qur'an to him, is his protector and helper, so their hostility does not frighten him in the least.

### Phrase by phrase

**"“Indeed, my Protector is Allah"** The word rendered "protector" also means helper. It is the One in charge of his affairs, who keeps him safe so that he needs no one besides Him. Allah's support is enough for him. Allah is his supporter, in whom he trusts and with whom he takes refuge. In this world and the next He guards him, as He will guard every righteous believer who comes after. So he fears nothing from their idols.

**"Who has revealed this Book."** The Book is the Holy Qur'an. Allah sent Jibrīl (Gabriel) to him with the Scripture, as guidance for people.

**"For He ˹alone˺ protects the righteous"** He takes charge of the righteous, protecting them, keeping them safe and helping them. These are those among His creation who do good. According to Ibn ʿAbbās, "the righteous" here means all who set up no one as equal to Allah, prophets and faithful Muslims alike.

### Why mention the revelation of the Book?

Of all Allah's attributes, this verse names in particular His revealing the Book to the Prophet ﷺ. The only reason for the idolaters' hostility was that he called them to the message of the Qur'an. So he could be sure that Allah, who had revealed it, would help and protect him.

Ibrāhīm al-Khalīl, the Friend of Allah, declared the same reliance. He told his people: "Have you ˹really˺ considered what you have been worshipping—you and your ancestors? They are ˹all˺ enemies to me, except the Lord of all worlds. ˹He is˺ the One Who created me, and He ˹alone˺ guides me" (26:75-78). He also said to his father and his people: "I am totally free of whatever ˹gods˺ you worship except the One Who originated me, and He will surely guide me.” And he left this enduring declaration among his descendants, so they may ˹always˺ turn back ˹to Allah˺" (43:26-28).

### Can enemies harm the righteous?

The closing words give a general rule. Allah helps and protects not only His messengers, who hold the highest rank, but every Muslim who acts righteously. So no one's opposition or hostility can harm a true Muslim in the real sense. Very often he is made to triumph over his enemies in this world. If, for some good reason, he does not prevail and seems defeated, even that does not damage his real aim. His failure in this world is in fact success, because the aim of his life is to seek Allah's pleasure and obey Him in everything. A setback that comes from Allah only brings him closer to that aim.

### In short

- The Prophet ﷺ did not fear the idolaters, since Allah, who revealed the Qur'an to him, was his protector.
- The revelation is mentioned because the Qur'an's message was the cause of their hostility.
- Allah protects all the righteous, so even an apparent defeat is, for a true Muslim, a step toward Allah's pleasure.

197.text:
The Prophet ﷺ goes on: "But those ˹false gods˺ you call besides Him can neither help you nor even themselves.”" This repeats what was said earlier (7:192), but this time as a direct address to the idolaters. Since their gods can do nothing, why should he be concerned with them?

### Phrase by phrase

**"But those ˹false gods˺ you call besides Him"**: the idols you call on and worship besides Allah, O idolaters.

**"can neither help you"** They have no power to benefit or harm you.

**"nor even themselves.”"** They cannot even stop what is done to them. They are utterly incapable of doing anything. So how can you call on them instead of calling on Allah?

### What counts as an idol?

This is not limited to the familiar kinds of idol. It is the state of everything given the status of an object of worship. That includes one's native land and community, and personalities, living or dead, who attract feelings that belong only to Allah, the One. All these fall into the same category, since giving them such feelings amounts to treating them as divine.

What is the reality of all these things? None has power of its own. None made its own legs, hands or eyes. Everyone with legs was given them, and if a leg is taken away he cannot make another. Everyone with hands was given them, and if a hand is lost he cannot make another. Everyone with eyes received them as a gift, and if an eye is lost he cannot make himself a new one.

Allah alone is humankind's Sustainer and Saviour. In this world He is unseen, but in the Hereafter He will reveal Himself. Then people will see with their own eyes that Allah alone provided for and sustained them. Only their foolishness led them to credit this to imagined deities. Those partners cannot even look after themselves, so what can they do for others? Allah alone helps His servants in this world, and He will help His faithful servants in the world to come.

### In short

- The false gods cannot help their worshippers, or even protect themselves.
- Anything given worship-like devotion, whether land, community or a person, is helpless in the same way, since none made its own limbs.
- Allah alone sustains and helps, and in the Hereafter everyone will see it plainly.

198.text:
The idols look as if they see, but they are blind: "If you ˹idolaters˺ call them to guidance, they cannot hear. And you ˹O Prophet˺ may see them facing towards you, but they cannot see". The idolaters used to make statues in the shape of people and animals, with hands, feet and eyes. Yet these were only objects, lifeless and unable to move.

### Phrase by phrase

**"If you ˹idolaters˺ call them to guidance, they cannot hear."** Call the idols you serve in place of Allah to steadfastness and the right path, and they will not hear the call. One explanation takes the address as being to the Muslims calling the idols to the truth. Either way, the idols neither hear nor answer, because they are not living but dead. The point was made before, with the verse quoted under 7:193 (35:14).

**"And you ˹O Prophet˺ may see them facing towards you,"** You see the idols, O Muhammad, staring at you with their eyes open and painted on, looking toward you as a person looks.

**"but they cannot see"** They perceive nothing, because they are not living but dead. They are objects that cannot see!

### Why does the verse speak of idols as if they were people?

The idols have eyes that stare as if they could see, though they are solid. So the verse speaks of them as though they had minds. It says tarāhum, the form used for rational beings, and not tarāhā, the form used for things. This is because they are made in human shape, with eyes drawn on them.

### In short

- Idols called to guidance cannot hear, because they are lifeless.
- Their carved and painted eyes seem to look at the Prophet ﷺ, but they see nothing.
- The verse speaks of them as if they had minds only because they were shaped like people.

199.text:
After describing the stubborn ignorance and bad conduct of Islam's opponents, the Qur'an gives the Prophet ﷺ a contrasting code of conduct: "Be gracious, enjoin what is right, and turn away from those who act ignorantly". This verse is a complete code and model of moral excellence. Through it the Holy Prophet ﷺ was trained, and he was given the distinction, unique among all humankind, of embodying every moral excellence.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Be gracious,"** Literally, "take what is pardoned", khudh al-ʿafw. The word ʿafw has many meanings, and any of them may be meant here, which is why interpreters of the Qur'an have explained it in different ways. The most widely agreed meaning is something done easily, without difficulty. So the phrase means: accept from people what comes easily to them. Accept what issues naturally from people's manners and conduct, and do not scrutinise them. Do not ask them to do what is too hard for them, since that will drive them away. Another meaning of ʿafw is pardon and forgiveness, and some interpreters take it that way. On their view, the Prophet ﷺ is told to pardon people's mistakes and shortcomings. One explanation took it to mean the surplus wealth of one's family and dependents, a ruling later abrogated.

**"enjoin what is right,"** The word is al-ʿurf, which al-Bukhārī explained as righteousness. It means "the recognised": everything done in a good and praiseworthy way, kindness, decency and benevolence. He should tell people to speak beautifully and do good. The sense is that he should not avenge the oppression of his enemies but forgive them, while still urging them to do what is good and beneficial. So he would not merely repay evil with good and injustice with justice. He would repay it all with a higher degree of grace, that of iḥsān. Calling people to the oneness of Allah, the Hereafter, a virtuous life and justice is calling them to ʿurf, to deeds whose goodness reason itself can confirm.

**"and turn away from those who act ignorantly"** He should give up revenge, deal with his enemies in goodwill and concern, and explain the truth to them gently. But some ignorant diehards will be unmoved even by this gentle response, and will show yet more ignorance and harshness. He is told not to let their wounding remarks and crude challenges affect him, and not to answer them in their own terms. He should keep away from them and ignore them. Whoever harms him, he should not harm. Turning away also means not repaying evil with evil. It does not mean he should stop advising them, since that would not befit the mission of a prophet and messenger of Allah. One explanation names the ignorant as Abū Jahl and his people, who mocked the Prophet ﷺ, and says this turning away was later abrogated.

### "Accept what comes easily"

The prayer, ṣalāh, illustrates the first meaning. Its true spirit is to set aside every worldly thought and act and stand before one's Lord in perfect reverence. The worshipper offers his praise as though speaking to his Lord directly, making his requests to Him with nothing and no one in between. This state shows itself in signs of submission and humility, khushūʿ and khuḍūʿ, which only a few fortunate worshippers reach. Such reverence and love cannot be expected of every worshipper. So the Holy Prophet ﷺ was told not to demand the highest standard from people, but to accept whatever degree of excellence they could easily reach.

Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī records this meaning. In it, ʿAbdullāh ibn az-Zubayr is reported, through his brother ʿUrwah and ʿUrwah's son Hishām, as saying the verse concerned nothing but people's character. Similar reports come through Hishām from Ibn ʿUmar and from ʿĀʾishah, and Allah knows best. Hishām ibn ʿUrwah reported his father saying that Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to pardon people their behaviour. Mujāhid, in more than one narration, said it means pardoning people's conduct and deeds. Another report says that when this verse was revealed, the Holy Prophet ﷺ said he had been commanded to accept ordinary obedience from people in their worship and conduct, and would do so as long as he was among them. Many interpreters of the Qur'an, including ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, ʿAbdullāh ibn az-Zubayr, ʿĀʾishah and Mujāhid, confirmed this meaning.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to forgive the idolaters and turn away from them for ten years, after which He ordered him to be firm with them.

### "Forgive whoever wrongs you"

Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, through Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, that Umay said that when Allah revealed this verse, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked Jibrīl (Gabriel) what it meant. Jibrīl first confirmed the meaning with Allah. Then he said that Allah commanded him to forgive whoever wronged him, give to whoever withheld from him, and keep ties with whoever cut them off.

Ibn Marduwaih reported from Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah that the verse came down after the battle of Uḥud. Ḥamzah had been martyred there and his body savagely mutilated. Seeing him in that state, the Holy Prophet ﷺ said he would treat seventy of their men as they had treated Ḥamzah. This verse was then revealed, telling him that such revenge did not suit his noble station, and that he should pardon and forgive.

Imām Aḥmad supports this with a hadith from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir. The Holy Prophet ﷺ taught him the same: to pardon whoever wrongs him, keep ties with whoever cuts him off, and give to whoever deprives him. Al-Bayhaqī also reported from ʿAlī that the Holy Prophet ﷺ said he would teach him manners better than those of all earlier and later peoples. He should give to whoever deprives him, pardon whoever wrongs him, and keep ties with whoever breaks with him.

The two meanings of ʿafw differ, but their essence is one. He should not demand the highest standard of worship and conduct from people. He should pardon their mistakes, take no revenge for their wrongs, and be generous to them without expecting anything in return.

### How did the Prophet ﷺ live this verse?

The authentic records of his life show that the Holy Prophet ﷺ gave the truest picture of this Qur'anic model of conduct. It reached full flower at the conquest of Makkah, when the enemies who had sworn to destroy him lay at his mercy. He set them all free. Far from seeking revenge for their injustices, he said, he would not even blame them for anything that had passed between them.

### ʿUmar and the verse

Al-Bukhārī recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās that during ʿUmar's caliphate, ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn ibn Ḥudhayfah came to Madinah and stayed with his nephew, al-Ḥurr ibn Qays. Al-Ḥurr was one of the learned men whom ʿUmar kept near him. ʿUmar liked to have those who knew the Qur'an by heart close to him and to consult them, whether they were old or young. ʿUyaynah told his nephew that he was close to the Commander of the Faithful, Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and asked him to get him a meeting. Al-Ḥurr asked ʿUmar, and ʿUmar gave permission.

Once in the presence of ʿUmar al-Fārūq, ʿUyaynah spoke rudely and untruthfully. "O Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb," he said, "you neither give us enough nor judge fairly among us." ʿUmar grew so angry that he almost punished him. Then al-Ḥurr said: "O Commander of the Faithful, Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ, 'Be gracious, enjoin what is right, and turn away from those who act ignorantly.' This man is one of the ignorant." By Allah, once ʿUmar heard the verse recited he did nothing more. He was one who stopped at the limits of Allah's Book. It was well known of him that he readily yielded to the commands of the Book of Allah, the Mighty, the Exalted.

### Two kinds of people

This verse gathers the noble traits of character. Some scholars sum it up this way. People are of two kinds. One kind does good. Accept their good deeds as they are, do not pry or ask more than they can bear, and do not demand the very best from them. The other kind falls short or does wrong. Teach them what is good and show them the way of righteousness. If they still refuse, cling to their error and speak arrogantly and aggressively, the right course is to keep away and not answer their ignorant talk. Ignoring them may avert their harm, and it is hoped that this may one day bring them round, when they realise their error.

### What should a caller to the truth do?

People find an upright life very hard. The desire for quick gain pulls them toward worldly profit, and they often exploit religion for worldly ends. When the call to pure truth reaches them, they fear for their interests and oppose it with all their might. In such a situation the only right response for the caller, the dāʿī, is avoidance. He should go on spreading the message without stirring up clashes or confrontation. Otherwise daʿwah turns into debate, and his time and energy are wasted arguing with those he addresses. To keep the call pure, the dāʿī must stay patient in every unpleasant situation and carry on his work in a positive way.

### The inner reading: the generous Lord's command

The command came from the generous, lovingly kind Lord, Lord of all lords and masters, generous and gentle in name and sign. It came to Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, whom the world's people follow. O master, pass over the sins of the sinners, cover their faults, and draw the pen of pardon across the record of wrongdoers. O master, take from Allah a pleasing character, praiseworthy conduct, truthful speech and peace with people. Be the friend of the good in company and attend to them in solitude.

Allah is a forbearing Lord who loves the forbearing. He hears the unworthy words of His enemies and sees their insolence in private, yet keeps the curtain drawn over them. He does not hurry to punish. He offers them repentance and pardon and calls them back to His threshold, as He says: "Tell the disbelievers that if they desist, their past will be forgiven." (8:38).

A tradition has Allah saying: "You called on Me, and I said, 'Here I am!' You asked of Me, and I gave to you. You rose against Me, and I gave you respite." He goes on: "You left Me, and I took care of you. You disobeyed Me, and I covered you. So if you return to Me, I will accept you, and if you turn away, I will wait for you." And He says: "I am the most munificent of the munificent and the most generous of the generous." Another report says that when an old man repents, Allah says: "Now? When your strength is gone and your appetite cut off? Yet I am the Most Merciful of the merciful, the Most Merciful of the merciful."

### In short

- The verse gives the Prophet ﷺ a complete moral code: accept what comes easily from people and pardon them, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.
- Jibrīl explained it as forgiving whoever wrongs you, giving to whoever withholds from you and keeping ties with whoever cuts you off.
- The Prophet ﷺ lived it most fully at the conquest of Makkah, and ʿUmar's anger subsided the moment the verse was recited to him.
- Callers to the truth should keep calling patiently and avoid confrontation with those who answer with ignorance.

200.text:
The previous verse asked for something hard: forgiving the wrongs of the unjust and the ignorant and not answering evil with evil. This verse completes it: "If you are tempted by Satan, then seek refuge with Allah. Surely He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing". Such forbearance is very hard on human nature. On just such occasions Satan is at hand to provoke even a calm person to anger and get him ready to fight. So when anger flares while one's patience is being tested, one should recognise at once that the prompting comes from Satan. Its standard treatment is to seek refuge with Allah.

### Phrase by phrase

**"If you are tempted by Satan,"** If Satan stirs you with a whisper or a doubt, tries to bring you an evil suggestion, or turns you away from what you were commanded to do. In the Arabic, "if" (in) is merged with an added "any" (mā) to form immā. Ibn Jarīr explained: if the devil lures you to anger, turning you away from forgiving the ignorant and toward punishing him.

**"then seek refuge with Allah."** Ask Allah for protection from his whispering and take refuge with Him, and He will ward it off from you. The fuller sense is left implied. Allah commands seeking refuge with Him from the devil's whispers. The hadiths on istiʿādhah, seeking refuge, are not repeated here.

**"Surely He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing"** He hears your seeking refuge with Him and whatever you say, and He knows the devil's whispering and what is done. Ibn Jarīr said Allah hears the ignorance that fools inflict on you, your seeking refuge with Him, and all the speech of His creation, none of which escapes Him. He knows what drives the devil's lures away from you, and everything else His creatures do.

### Words that remove anger

A hadith tells of two men quarrelling in front of the Holy Prophet ﷺ. One of them was losing control in his anger. The Prophet ﷺ looked at him and said he knew words that would take his rage away if he said them: "I seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed." When the man heard the Holy Prophet ﷺ say this, he repeated it at once, and his anger vanished.

### Three verses that end in seeking refuge

There is a remarkable pattern here. Three verses in the whole Qur'an embody high moral teaching, and all three end with the need to seek refuge from Satan. These three passages, in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, Sūrat al-Muʾminūn and Sūrat as-Sajdah, are unique in the Qur'an. One is this verse. The second is in Sūrat al-Muʾminūn: "Respond to evil with what is best. We know well what they claim. And say, “My Lord! I seek refuge in You from the temptations of the devils. And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, that they ˹even˺ come near me.”" (23:96-98).

The third is in Sūrah Ḥā Mīm as-Sajdah, also called Fuṣṣilat, verses 34 to 36: "Good and evil cannot be equal. Respond ˹to evil˺ with what is best, then the one you are in a feud with will be like a close friend. But this cannot be attained except by those who are patient and who are truly fortunate. And if you are tempted by Satan, then seek refuge with Allah. Indeed, He ˹alone˺ is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing" (41:34-36). Verse 35 adds that only the patient and the truly fortunate reach this. The last of these verses (41:36) is worded almost exactly like the verse of al-Aʿrāf.

### Why is Satan mentioned after forgiveness?

All three verses teach people to overlook and forgive those who provoke their anger, to return good for evil, and at the same time to seek refuge from Satan. Allah encourages gentle treatment of wrongdoers, since it may deter them from persisting in their wrong, Allah willing. But the devil is not deterred by gentleness, because he wants a person's total ruin. He is humankind's open enemy, as he was the enemy of their father Adam before them. So the remedy against him is refuge with Allah.

This shows that Satan takes a special interest in human quarrels. Whenever a quarrel breaks out, the devils converge on it as their favourite hunting ground. However calm and forbearing a person may be, they will still try to inflame him and push him beyond the limits. The treatment is this. Once someone notices his temper slipping beyond control, he should understand that Satan is gaining the upper hand over his better self, turn to Allah and seek refuge with Him. This lets noble traits of character flourish at their best. That is why the next two verses lay further stress on seeking Allah's protection against Satan.

### In short

- Forgiving wrongs is hard, and Satan uses such moments to inflame anger, so the cure is to seek refuge with Allah.
- The Prophet ﷺ taught an angry man to say, "I seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed", and his anger left him.
- Three Qur'anic passages on returning good for evil all end with seeking refuge from Satan, who loves to exploit quarrels.

201.text:
Those who fear Allah are quickly alerted when Satan approaches: "Indeed, when Satan whispers to those mindful ˹of Allah˺, they remember ˹their Lord˺ then they start to see ˹things˺ clearly". Allah describes His servants who have taqwā, obeying His commands and avoiding what He forbids.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, when Satan whispers to those mindful ˹of Allah˺,"** When an evil thought, anger, or Satan's whispering crosses their minds, or a doubt or insinuation reaches them, or they intend to do wrong or commit an error. The word is ṭayf, "a visitation", with a variant reading ṭāʾif. These are those who guard against the devil's whispers.

**"they remember ˹their Lord˺"** They remember Allah's might, His punishment of wrongdoers and His immense reward for those who do good. They remember His promises and threats, and they come to know Allah's guidance. Then they repent and turn back to Him, seeking refuge with Him and asking His forgiveness before death.

**"then they start to see ˹things˺ clearly"** They become upright and see the error of their ways. They tell truth from falsehood, hold back from transgression and turn their faces back to Allah.

### Sensitivity, the believer's shield

No one in this world is safe from the attacks of the self and of Satan. What saves a person on all such occasions is the fear of Allah. Fear of Allah makes one extremely sensitive, and this sensitivity is the greatest shield in this world of trial. Whenever an evil thought enters his mind, or a negative mood takes hold of him, his sensitivity warns him at once. His eyes open immediately. He asks Allah's forgiveness and resolves never to commit such wrong again.

### In short

- When Satan whispers to those who fear Allah, they remember Allah's punishment and reward, His promises and threats.
- They then see clearly, repent and turn back to Him.
- Fear of Allah makes a person sensitive, and that sensitivity is his shield against the self and Satan.

202.text:
The opposite is the state of Satan's companions: "But the devils persistently plunge their ˹human˺ associates deeper into wickedness, sparing no effort". Those who have no fear of Allah have no such shield.

### Phrase by phrase

**"But the devils persistently plunge their ˹human˺ associates"** Their brothers are the devils' brothers among humankind, the disbelievers who commit immorality. They follow the devils, listen to them and obey their orders. The verse quoted under 7:31 (17:27) calls the wasteful brothers of the devils. One explanation reverses it: the brothers of the idolaters, meaning the devils, drag the idolaters along with their insinuations.

**"deeper into wickedness,"** The devils help them commit sins, making that path easy and attractive to them. They draw them into ever greater error, into disbelief, error and sin, one sin after another.

**"sparing no effort"** The devils never stop urging people to do wrong. Ibn ʿAbbās, as ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah reported, said that neither do humans stop short of the evil they are doing, nor do the devils stop luring them. So "sparing no effort" means the devils never tire or cease their whispering. Neither the devils in their misleading nor the immoral who follow them ever stop. Unlike those who fear Allah, these people never come to see clearly. Allah says in another verse: "Do you ˹O Prophet˺ not see that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, constantly inciting them" (19:83). Ibn ʿAbbās and others explained this as the devils constantly luring the disbelievers into evil.

### Why do some never wake up?

A heart emptied of the fear of Allah keeps no watch against Satan. Step by step he draws such people toward the pit of ruin, and they never notice. Sensitivity is a person's greatest shield, while insensitivity leaves him defenceless against Satan's attacks.

### In short

- The devils keep drawing their human brothers, the immoral and the disbelievers, deeper into error.
- Neither the devils nor their followers ever stop, and those followers never come to see clearly.
- A heart without the fear of Allah is defenceless and is led to destruction unawares.

203.text:
The idolaters met every sign with a demand for another: "If you ˹O Prophet˺ do not bring them a sign ˹which they demanded˺, they ask, “Why do you not make it yourself?”" The Prophet ﷺ is told how to answer: "Say, “I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. This ˹Quran˺ is an insight from your Lord—a guide and a mercy for those who believe.”" The verse offers proof that the Holy Prophet ﷺ is the true Messenger of Allah and answers the doubts of his opponents. When he brought a sign they rejected it, and when he did not, they asked why he had not produced one.

### Phrase by phrase

**"If you ˹O Prophet˺ do not bring them a sign ˹which they demanded˺,"** When you do not bring the people of Makkah one of the miracles they ask for. "Sign" here means a miracle. Allah says elsewhere: "If We willed, We could send down upon them a ˹compelling˺ sign from the heavens, leaving their necks bent in ˹utter˺ submission to it" (26:4).

**"they ask, “Why do you not make it yourself?”"** Ibn ʿAbbās, as ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah reported, explained it as: why have you not been given a miracle? Or: why have you not brought one about or made it yourself? Ibn Jarīr reported Mujāhid's reading, that they were telling him to come up with a miracle himself. Qatādah, as-Suddī, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and Ibn Jarīr held the same view. One explanation gives: why do you not take it on yourself to bring it from Allah? Another gives: why do you not invent it yourself? The pagans were asking why he did not strive to bring them a miracle from Allah that they could witness and believe in.

**"Say, “I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord."** I do and say only what my Lord reveals to me, and it is not for me to bring anything of my own accord. The Prophet ﷺ was to say that he does not ask his Lord for such things. He only follows what Allah reveals and commands him. If Allah sends a miracle, he will accept it. Otherwise he will not ask for one unless Allah permits him. Surely Allah is All-Wise, All-Knowing.

**"This ˹Quran˺ is an insight from your Lord"** Allah then points His servants to the Qur'an itself as the mightiest miracle, the plainest evidence, and the truest proof and explanation. It is a collection of proofs and miracles from your Lord, your Creator, who arranges your lives. It sets out commands and prohibitions. Whoever reflects on it, even briefly, cannot leave it without believing that it is the Word of Allah alone, and that nothing created had any part in it.

**"—a guide and a mercy for those who believe.”"** It guides people out of error and is a mercy that shields them from punishment. The Qur'an is a proof of the truth for the whole world. But it leads to the purpose of life, and to Allah's mercy, only for those who believe in it. Those who do not believe are lost and wretched.

### Why were their demands not met?

To prove that they are messengers of Allah, all the prophets were given miracles. In keeping with this, the Holy Prophet ﷺ, the foremost of the prophets, was blessed with miracles that outnumber those of earlier prophets and are just as clear. His miracles, established by the Qur'an and authentic hadith reports, are many. Muslim scholars have written whole books on them. One well-known work on the subject is as-Suyūṭī's two-volume al-Khaṣāʾiṣ al-Kubrā. Yet despite so many miracles, his opponents kept making unreasonable demands for new miracles of their own choosing. Such demands appear earlier in this surah too.

The verse answers their demand on principle. A prophet's miracle is testimony and proof of his mission. Suppose a plaintiff's claim is proved by trustworthy evidence, and the other side has not challenged it. No court in the world would let that side insist that it will accept the claim only if evidence comes from certain people it names, while leaving the existing evidence unchallenged. In the same way, after seeing so many clear miracles, his opponents had no right to say they would accept him as Allah's Messenger only if he produced miracles made to their order. That was simply a hostile demand that no court of justice would accept.

So when he did not show them the miracle they specified, they used it as an excuse to deny that he was Allah's Messenger. Had he been one, they said, he would have shown them the miracle they chose. The Holy Prophet ﷺ was told to answer that his mission was not to produce miracles on his own. His basic task was to follow the commands his Lord sent him through revelation, waḥy, and to preach them, and he was busy doing what he had been assigned. The miracles they had already seen were more than enough to confirm his status. Having seen them, their demand for a particular miracle was mere hostility, not worth attention.

Among all his miracles, the Qur'an is itself a great miracle. It challenged the whole world to produce even a short surah like it, and the world failed. That is open proof that the Qur'an is not human speech but the inimitable Word of Allah, the Most Exalted.

### In short

- When the Prophet ﷺ did not produce the miracles they demanded, the idolaters asked why he did not make one himself.
- He was told to say that he follows only what is revealed, and asks for no sign without Allah's permission.
- Having seen many miracles, they had no right to demand others to order, just as no court would allow such a demand.
- The Qur'an itself is the greatest miracle, insight from Allah and a guide and mercy for believers.

204.text:
After Allah described the Qur'an as clear evidence, guidance and mercy, He commanded that it be listened to whenever it is recited, out of respect and honour for it: "When the Quran is recited, listen to it attentively and be silent, so you may be shown mercy". The Holy Qur'an has come as a mercy for the believers. But to benefit from that mercy there are conditions and rules of conduct, and this verse states them as a general command.

### Phrase by phrase

**"When the Quran is recited,"** One explanation says this refers to recitation in the prescribed prayers. Another says it was revealed about keeping silent during the sermon in the mosque, called "the Qur'an" here because the sermon contains it. Others say it concerns silence and attention whenever the Qur'an is recited.

**"listen to it attentively"** Lend your ears to its recitation and pay heed. Do not talk, and do not busy yourself with anything else. Listening here includes not only hearing it but obeying it and striving to act on its commands.

**"and be silent,"**: refraining from speech while it is being recited.

**"so you may be shown mercy"** Do this so that Allah may have mercy on you and you are not punished. These closing words make it clear that the Qur'an's mercy depends on observing this etiquette. By the same token, whoever flouts these rules and shows disrespect to the Qur'an deserves Allah's wrath, not His mercy.

### Why was this command given?

This command runs against the practice of the pagans of Quraysh, who said: "Do not listen to this Quran but drown it out so that you may prevail." (41:26). Ibn Jarīr reported that Ibn Masʿūd said they used to greet one another with salām during the prayer, and then this verse was revealed.

There are different reports about the background of these verses. They differ over whether the command concerns recitation in the prayer, in the sermon (khuṭbah), or recitation of any kind, in prayer, sermon or anywhere else. According to most scholars, the correct view is that the verse's words are general, so its rule too applies generally, except on some particular occasions.

### Does the follower recite behind the imam?

The followers of the Ḥanafī school take this verse as proof that those praying behind an imam should not recite. Even the jurists who tell followers to recite al-Fātiḥah behind the imam have kept this verse in view. They say the follower should recite only when the imam pauses. This is not the place to pursue that debate, which is treated in the standard works of the scholars.

The main point of the verse is that those for whom the Qur'an is declared a mercy must recognise the etiquette and respect it is owed, and observe it in practice. The chief etiquette is that listeners give it their ears when it is recited and stay silent.

### Silence in prayer and in the sermon
